Hannah and Cade are unwinding in the sunken hot tub. Black is in his customary spot with his back to the house. Behind him, the pool and patio area are bustling with activity, typical for a Sunday morning. About two dozen resident subordinates are moving about in the vicinity, cleaning up after the Saturday night party.

The brawny Farrin is busy skimming the pool since the need for security detail is minimal during brunch. Jayla, the masseuse, is spraying solution on the massage table nearby him. Black’s sub Kaime realigns the poolside lounge chairs while his other sub Kayleigh follows her, wiping them off as they move down the row.

“Chelsea wasn’t feeling well enough to work this morning.” Cade explains the absence of one of his own subs.

“That’s funny, because she seemed perfectly fine last night at the party.” Hannah picks up her near-empty glass of orange juice and drinks the last sip. She puts the glass down behind her next to her banana peel.

“She probably drank too much.”

Hannah wrinkles her nose at Cade’s tolerance. “Hell, Brian didn’t even get to attend the party last night, and he’s cleaning a guest room right now. Nobody wants that task.”

“That’s only because he serves under you.” Cade counters.

Will passes by in the background, heading for the hot tub. He stoops down to collect Hannah’s empty glass and banana peel.

“Don’t make me out as a tyrant.” She spars back at Cade.

“Don’t need me for that, beautiful.”

Behind Cade, over by the fire pit, Marsa scoops ashes out of the pit. She shovels them into the paper sack that Minya is holding open for her. The twins are casually dressed with their hair pulled back.

Cade turns to Black. “I have some conversation points for your talk with Jane today.”

“No.” Black addresses Cade with explicit disdain. “I don’t want your points.” Behind Black, the bartender Ryan carries a tray of empty glasses to the patio door. The redheaded Spinner is coming out of the house, lugging a container of cleaning supplies.

“Just humor me.”

“Cade, this is what I do. Hijacking levelheaded potential subs is my job here.”

“I know that, but–”

Black cuts him off with a flat, “No.” Then he reaches back to pick up his phone. “Turn the jets off for a second.” He pulls up Jane’s number.

“You forgot to call her, didn’t you?” Cade bends over to the control panel and shuts off the jets.

Black raises his phone up to his ear, waiting for her to answer.

“Hello?”

“Jane, are we still meeting for lunch?”

“I can, yes.” She sounds stirred. “Who is this?”

“Why don’t you meet me at the Italian restaurant on Jackson Street? It’s not far from your place.”

“Yeah, Maria’s, I’m familiar with it.”

“See you at noon.”

“Who do I look for?”

Black ends the call. The hot tub jets fire back up.

***

Right at noon, Jane stands in the entrance of Maria’s, a quaint Italian restaurant. The décor is simple, but with a traditional Italian-style flair. Jane scans the dining room full of occupied tables.

“Hi there.” A hostess greets her. “Can I help you?”

“Well, I’m meeting a man here.” And that’s really all Jane knows.

“Okay, this table right up front here is expecting another. Or.” She points at a table along the wall. “Is that the gentleman you’re looking for?”

“Yes, thank you,” Jane answers as though she isn’t unsure as hell. She heads for the table. It’s tucked in next to an ivy-draped column. She centers on the trim, dark-haired guy sitting with his back to the wall. He sets his phone on the table.

Jane approaches the table, smiling. “Hi.” She leans over the back of the chair across from him. “I don’t know you, and you may not know me, but by any chance–”

“Jane, have a seat.”

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.content:
Chapter 2

Jane’s hands are resting on the back of the chair across the table from Black.

“Sit down.” He repeats, welcoming her.

Her pause suggests that Black’s voice in person is resonating with Jane, transporting her back to a dark moment from that night. It’s the same snide voice that asked, “No one’s ever treated you like this before, have they?”

As she sits down in the chair, Jane comes to the distinct realization that she’s seated across from one of her abductors. “You sound familiar.”

“We spoke on the phone a little bit ago.”

“No. I mean, you were there that night.”

“For a while I was.” Black affirms. Then he wryly asks, “So how have you been?”

“All right, I guess,” Jane answers with an uncomfortable laugh. She glimpses at Black. “But it’s not you? Behind this, I mean?”

“Nope,” he tells her. “I’m just doing a favor for the person who is behind this.”

“Okay.” Jane replies pensively.

“I took the liberty of ordering for us. You can’t really go wrong with Italian, can you?”

“Not usually.”

Black’s self-assurance comes off as intimidating, but it doesn’t deter Jane. She notices the glass of iced tea on the table in front of her and has a sip.

“And this lunch is your first clue.” Black stops talking when a waitress drops off their salads. Jane grabs her white cotton napkin and places it over her lap. “Thank you,” Black says to the waitress. He reaches for his fork and picks up where he left off. “Knowing my identity obviously doesn’t matter at this point. Add that to your list of things that you do know.”

Jane reels back, and Black carries on.

“And by seeing you here today, I have to assume that you’re interested in what this person has to offer you.”

“I definitely have a lot of questions.”

“I’m sure you do.” Black huffs out a short laugh. He stabs a bite of his salad.

“So who are you, then?”

“I’m Black.”

“No, you’re not,” she says plainly.

He rolls his eyes at her wit and eats his bite of salad.

Baring a coy smile, Jane pulls a slice of Italian bread from the basket on their table. “Is that a code name of some kind?” She tears off a small piece of bread and pops it into her mouth.

“Sort of. Bottom line, you don’t know the guy who’s behind this.”

“Does this guy have a name?”

“Of course he has a name, but we’re not that far along yet.” Black responds in a blunt manner and resumes eating his salad.

“Well yeah, since names are usually like the last thing you learn about someone.” She jokes, tearing off another piece of bread.

“He’s a complete stranger to you. So, it’s pointless to say much more until you meet him.”

“That opens up another good question.” Jane drags the hunk of bread through the pool of Italian dressing on her salad plate.

“When will you meet him? It hasn’t been determined.”

“But,” she attempts to repress the sheer eagerness that creeps into her throat, “I will, right?”

Jane’s concern brings a small smirk to Black’s face. He sets down his fork. “Of course you will. I just can’t tell you exactly when.” He shrugs. “That one’s out of my hands, sorry.”

“Can you tell me why he chose me?”

“He just had a hunch about you. And he decided to take the backdoor approach at introducing himself.”

“The backdoor approach?”

The waitress arrives with their meals. She delivers a plate of lasagna to each of them.

After a satisfied nod at the waitress, Black leans back in his chair. “It’s the opposite of the typical approach. Normally, you’d meet, decide if you’re attracted and then follow the customary path of getting to know one another. At some point in time, you’d encounter each other’s true selves, and from there it’s a toss-up. You either make the effort and move forward, or you get out. Right?”

“More or less,” she answers.

Black picks up his knife and fork. He begins cutting into the lasagna. “Everybody has an alter ego, a dark side, whatever you want to call it. It can take years for that to surface, though.” He pierces his fork into a piece of lasagna and adds, “People can be so insecure.” With a dispassionate frown, Black chews his bite of lasagna.

Jane smiles at him. Black’s warmly compelling vibe puts her at ease.

“Are you a Jung fan?” he asks her.

“If you mean Carl Jung, I’m familiar with him,” she answers, hands in her lap. Black has her attention. Jane’s plate of food looks to be the furthest thing from her mind.

“Then maybe you’re familiar with the true self versus the persona?”

“Mm-hmm, also referred to as the shadow self.”

“Have you ever met that side of somebody right off the bat?” Black cuts another piece of his lasagna.

“I don’t know.” She studies Black’s face. “Maybe I am right now.”

“Very observant.” He notes Jane’s probing lilt, as if she’s trying to dissect his method. He continues talking. Inducing words will keep her mind from wandering too far. “My alter ego is a lot more interesting than that over-analytical, detached guy. I don’t really go there very often anymore, if you know what I mean.” Black eats the bite of lasagna and puts his fork down.

“I think I do.”

“I’m sure you do. You strike me as an analyzer too, by the way.” His phone vibrates on the table. “Anyway, meeting somebody’s true self before their persona is the backdoor approach to a relationship.” He takes a drink of his iced tea.

A glint of doubt flashes in Jane’s eyes. “What kind of relationship are we talking about?”

“Ultimately, it can be whatever you want. There are no set rules or level of involvement.”

“Mm-hmm.” She hums in deliberation.

“The only thing, is you have to meet the true side of him first. Because in this game, the social mask doesn’t matter so much.” Black picks up his fork.

Jane arches her brows. “First it was a relationship and now it’s a game?”

“They’re one in the same.”

“Are they?” she asks cynically.

“They are. Eat up. Your lunch is getting cold.” Black points the prongs of his fork at Jane’s plate.

Somewhat flustered, she picks up her utensils and cuts a bite of lasagna.

“Playing the game just means accepting to go in the direction that this guy wants to take you. Really, it’s like any challenge life hands you but with different perks.” He sees Jane aim her twinkling eyes down at her plate. “And like I said, your level of involvement is entirely up to you. What you choose to label it is up to you.”

***

Meanwhile, Hannah and Cade are outside in the chaise lounge chairs by the Mercer Estate pool. They each have a plate of food containing an assortment of fresh fruit, quiche, pastry, fancy meats and cheeses. Cade piles slices of meat and cheese on a croissant, making it into a sandwich.

The pool is loud with activity, due to a water volleyball game in progress. Sporadic shouts and splashes are heard at an almost constant rate.

“I think your Spinner has a thing for Brian, by the way.” Hannah sticks her fork into a chunk of pineapple.

“She has a thing for everybody.” Cade grouses through an annoyed scowl.

Behind Hannah and Cade, a handful of unfamiliar faces trickle out of the house in the background. A couple waltzes up to them, Joe Parrish and his female companion Michelle, who was the target in the break-in-gone-bad debacle.

Joe Parrish is a clean cut, handsome guy in his late forties. His hair is peppered with grey, and he carries himself in a distinguished posture.

“How are you doing, Joe?” Cade greets him.

“Wonderful, thank you.”

“Well, well.” Hannah lowers her plate of Sunday brunch food to her chiffon sarong. “Look who’s still prowling around here this Sunday afternoon. Mister Joe Parrish, and this must be Michelle.” Though she’s heard the name Michelle numerous times over the past year, Joe just recently started bringing her to the house.

Joe introduces her to Hannah. “Michelle, this is Hannah Sedgwick.”

“It’s very nice to meet you, Hannah.”

“Did you have a good time last night?” A suggestive smile tugs at the corner of Hannah’s mouth. “I didn’t see much of you two at the party.”

Michelle returns Hannah’s smile while Joe responds.

“We did not see much of the party last night. But I’m sure it was incredible, as it always is.”

“Are you sticking around for brunch?”

“We had brunch.” Joe advises her. “We’re heading home. I just wanted to stop out here and say goodbye to the most scintillating woman in California.”

“Oh Joe.” Hannah dismissively waves off his admiration.

“She hates compliments.” Cade’s sarcasm is not lost on Joe.

He grins at Cade and gestures farewell to the two of them. “You take it easy.”

“I always do.” Hannah ensures him.

Joe places his hand on Michelle’s shoulder and steers her away from the pool area.

Hannah stabs her fork into a strawberry. “I’m glad Black wasn’t here for that. I have no desire to live that down again, so soon. You know?” She shifts her focus over to Cade. “What are you doing?”

Cade is sending a message on his phone. His plate of food rests on this thigh. “Texting him. Again.”

“How’s the lunch date going?”

“I don’t know, he’s not answering me.”

***

At Maria’s, Black’s phone is sitting on the table. It lights up and buzzes with a new message notification from Cade. Black pays no mind. He picks up the cloth napkin draped over his lap and tosses it onto his empty plate. “I’m really just here to get your questions out of the way and clear the path.”

Jane stares across the table at Black with trepidation. Her time window to obtain information is closing. The waitress delivers each of them a steaming cup of coffee.

“Thank you.” Black reaches for the sugar.

“Can I get you two anything else right now?”

“I don’t think so.” He glances over at Jane, who shakes her head in response.

The dutiful waitress leaves their table.

“Well, here’s a question,” Jane says tightly. Black notices the cagey pout on her face.

“What’s with the look?” He pours some sugar into his coffee cup and stirs it in.

“Did you guys hack into my computer?”

“No we did not.” Black puts his spoon down on the table.

“Then how did you link me to that story?”

He laughs at her. “You posted it on the internet.”

“Anonymously.” Jane specifies. She picks up a little metal container of creamer and pours some into her cup.

“You had to register on the site to post the story, right? We hacked the website, not your computer.”

“But I didn’t use my real name.”

“That doesn’t matter. You just trace the IP...” Black closes his eyes for a moment and scratches his temple. “Listen, we didn’t access your computer.” He picks up his coffee. “There are other ways to find things out about people.”

“Yeah, I’m sure.” Jane mutters, exhibiting her nagging sense of violation. “I’m sure you have your ‘ways’.”

Black sets down his coffee cup. He addresses her with a straightforward attitude and a cogent tone. “Listen, princess.”

Jane gazes up at him in surprise.

“You gave permission for this. Remember?” He challenges her.

“Of course I do.” She clicked a link and agreed to play. There’s no debating that.

“You brought yourself to this crossroad. You put out a request, and someone took you up on it.”

“But I didn’t know the specifics of how–”

“You didn’t want to know.” He interrupts her. “That’s irrelevant now, anyway. You went through degradation and yet you came back for more.” He bends in towards her. “Didn’t you, you little freak?”

His sharp words cut through Jane’s sensible façade. She gasps at the validity of his claim.

Black relaxes back in his chair. “So, you can hammer me with questions about your computer and your privacy concerns, or you can ask yourself why you called the number on the card. Why are you here today?” he casually asks. “How’d you get this far along in the game?”

Jane hangs her head, unable to deny her culpability. “Because I want to play it.”

“I know you do.”

She glances up at Black. He’s looking back at her with comforting eyes. Jane’s curiosity radiates.

“What do I do now?” She inquires and grows serious.

“I’ll let him know that you’re up for it, and you’ll be contacted.”

“I suppose that’s all you can tell me.”

“I can tell you that if you change your mind about all this, call that number on the card and leave a message saying, ‘no thank you’. No one answers that line, so you can leave it at any time. You won’t hear from us again.” Black takes one last drink of his coffee.

“No, I won’t be doing that.”

“Then wait for the call.” He sets down his coffee cup, grabs his phone and stands up from the table.

“You’re leaving?”

“It’s almost one, I’ve gotta go. The bill’s been paid, so leave whenever you’re ready.” Black shoots Jane a brief smile on his way to the door.

***

Cade lies back in his lounge chair, awaiting word from Black. He moves his empty brunch plate over to the vacant chaise beside him.

Hannah is over socializing with a few lingering party guests in the background.

Reno closes in on Cade’s chair with a plate of pizza. He’s wearing sunglasses and a baseball hat turned backwards. Covering his eyes and hair keeps him somewhat disguised. He has a seat in the lounge chair next to Cade.

“Decide to come out of hiding?” Cade ribs the bullish Top who regularly works scenario jobs.

“Yeah.” Reno scopes out the pool area, perturbed by the number of remaining guests. “There’s more people here than usual. It’s Sunday afternoon.”

“I know. Nobody seems to want to leave today.”

Reno holds up a slice of pizza. “I found some leftover pizza if you’re interested.”

“I already ate the fancy brunch shit.” Cade motions to his empty plate on the lounge chair beside him.

Nodding, Reno takes a bite of his pizza. A burst of cheers and howls carries over from the pool. The water volleyball game is still going on. Cade rests his hand on his phone, which is sitting on the arm of his chair. Reno eyeballs him.

“What are you doing?”

“Waiting to hear how the meeting with Jane is going.”

“She’s with Black, obviously?” He wolfs down his slice of pizza.

“Yes she is.” Cade’s phone begins to ring. “Finally.” He immediately answers the call, “Hey.”

“What is the matter with you?” Black’s irate voice blasts through the earpiece.

“I just wanted to see how things were going. You weren’t responding.”

“I was busy.”

“Yeah, I figured that. How’d it go?”

“Good. She wants to meet you.”

Flagrantly relieved, Cade slaps his palm over his forehead. “Ah, that’s perfect.” He lifts his hand. “Did she freak out about anything?”

“Privacy, but it was diffused.”

“Good, good.” Cade lowers his hand to the armrest. “Did you record it?”

“I did.”

“Okay, then I guess I’ll just wait until you get back to hear the...” Puzzled by the abrupt silence, Cade checks his phone and realizes Black has already hung up on him. He chuckles and sets his phone back down.

“All clear for round two with Jane?”

“All clear.”

“Good, I’m looking forward to that one.” Reno picks up another piece of pizza.

“You and me both.”

Random walks up to Cade and Reno. He stops at the foot of the lounge chair beside Reno.

“I just wish Trip would get back here.” Reno states while Random has a seat.

“Why,” Random presumes, “are you a little too busy these days?”

“Yeah, as a matter of fact.” He’s been helping out in Trip’s absence. “Shay has me booked on scenarios practically every other day.” Reno takes a bite of his pizza.

“Well, it’ll be a couple days before Trip gets back.” Random notifies him. “He’s taking a bus, evidently.”

“A bus?” Reno asks with his mouth full. “Why?”

“I’m not totally sure.”

“Hmm.” Reno swallows his bite. “That doesn’t sound like Trip. It sounds like some kind of act of concession, or...”

***

The Submission book is lying next to a bottle of water on the coffee table in Becky’s living room that afternoon. There’s a bookmark placed about halfway through the book. Her two phones are sitting further down the coffee table.

Becky plops down on the middle cushion of her couch. She reaches for the book and opens it up in her lap. Becky props her foot on the edge of the coffee table and starts reading.

Her old phone rings. She picks it up to look at the screen. “It’s really not a good time, mom.” Becky ignores the call, tosses her phone back down and keeps on reading.

A few seconds later, the old phone rings again.

“Seriously?” Becky sighs, sliding her bookmark into the book. She sets it on the couch cushion beside her and answers the phone. “Mom, what’s going on?”

“You know I hate it when you ignore my calls, Becky. Your father and I just got back from Houston.”

“Yeah, that’s right.” She sinks back into the couch cushion. Her impatience wanes. “How’s Uncle Gene?”

“He’s getting settled in at home.”

“That’s good. I’m glad to hear it.”

“Your aunt and I found some healthy casserole recipes, and we made up a bunch of stuff to put in the freezer to help out for a little while.”

“Sure.”

“What about you, honey? How’s work?”

“Work’s good.” Becky lets the lie flow. “Nothing really new to report.”

“How are things with Brian?”

“I’m actually not seeing Brian anymore.”

“Oh? When did that happen?”

“A week or two ago, it’s really no big deal,” Becky answers flippantly.

“Why is it no big deal? Are you dating somebody else?”

“Not in the traditional sense, no.”

“What in the world does that mean?” Becky’s mom asks through a laugh.

“It just means that there’s somebody I’m interested in, but I wouldn’t say we’re dating. I don’t have a status to put on it, that’s all.” Becky yields to the fact that she has no control over this situation whatsoever. She grazes her fingers across the book on the cushion beside her.

“What are your plans for the rest of the day?”

“I’m taking it easy today. There’s a book I’m trying to finish.”

“Anything I’ve heard of?”

Becky snorts and says, “No, I don’t think so.”

***

Later that evening, Black wanders into Cade’s office and finds him seated at his mahogany desk, rifling around a desk drawer. The warm sunset glows through the bay window behind Cade.

“It’s nice and quiet in here.” Black sits down in a leather armchair across the desk from him.

“Sunday night cleanup, you know?” Cade takes an ashtray out of his desk drawer and slides it over to Black, who sets an unlit joint down inside of it. “Everybody’s downstairs working.” He adds.

“Not everybody.” Black hints to him...

Right outside of Cade’s suite door, the Spinner is in the penthouse corridor across from Brian. She has her fingers laced together behind her back and her chest pushed out at him. “I’m very, very good at keeping secrets.” She swoops into Brian.

“So you’ve said.” Flattered by her proposition, Brian drags his feet for a moment before declining. “Listen, I’ve got to get back downstairs.”

“I promise it won’t take long.” The Spinner beseeches...

Inside the suite, Cade marches over to the door of his office and grips onto the doorframe. He leans out the doorway to yell at the Spinner. “Go to your room, right now!” He waits until he sees her sail into his suite from the corridor, then he pushes off the doorframe and turns around. “God.” Frustrated, Cade settles back into his desk chair and digs around his open desk drawer. He cools off quickly and continues speaking to Black in a rational mode. “I seriously need to unload that Spinner.” Cade pulls a box of notecards out of the drawer.

“Getting a little ahead of yourself, aren’t you?” Black sneers at him. “Jane’s on board, but I don’t see her moving in here anytime soon.”

Cade flips through the cards, selecting one with the scales of justice on the front of it. He also takes out a white envelope before slipping the box back into the drawer. “Well, you never know.”

“I have a good guess.” Black reaches for the joint in the ashtray and lights it.

Cade flips open the card and picks up a black felt-tip pen. “And besides,” he pulls off the cap, “I want to get rid of the Spinner either way.” Cade begins writing out the card. “I’ll need to eventually, here.”

“I know.” Black blows out a cloud of smoke. “Easier said than done.” He taps his joint into the ashtray.

“Tell me about it.” Cade looks up from the card at Black, sincerely appreciative. “Thanks again by the way, for doing this meeting with Jane today.” He resumes writing out the card. “You’re doing a great job.”

“She’s actually pretty easy.” Black admits and takes another hit of the joint.

“Still, you’re keeping this whole thing afloat. Don’t think I don’t recognize that.”

Black exhales and sets the joint in the ashtray. “I’m just counting up the absurd amount of favors I can call you in on down the road.”

“Oh, I’d do them anyway.” Cade pushes the card aside and picks up the white envelope. He writes ‘Jane’ on the front of the envelope and puts the cap back on the felt-tip pen.

Black glances at the envelope. “What’s Jane up to, tonight?”

Cade promptly picks up his phone. He brings up a GPS map and scans the screen. “She’s at a very exclusive restaurant,” he reports with a mischievous smile, “undoubtedly dining with her affluent family.”

***

After dinner, Jane is behind the wheel, alone in her white BMW. She’s on the phone with her tenacious younger sister, Julia.

“Where were you tonight, Jane?” Her snotty question blares through the car speakers.

“With you. Wh-what are you talking about?” Jane sputters, muddled by her sister’s grilling. She keeps her eyes on the road.

“Of course you were physically there, but you were not at Sunday dinner with the rest of us.”

“You know I hate it when dad goes on like that. You know that.”

“No, it was not your usual roll-your-eyes-at-dad, self. It was like you were somewhere else.”

“I don’t know what you’re getting at.” Jane tries putting the subject to rest.

“How’s everything going with school?”

“School’s good. I had a clinical on Friday.”

“Okay. So?” Julia waits for her to go on.

48 hours have gone by since the massage clinical that turned Jane’s world upside down and transported her into this enchanting game, in which she doesn’t even know who the puppet master is yet.

“What IS it?” Julia’s grinding impatience rips her sister out of her stupor.

“I don’t have anything to tell you.” Jane insists.

“So you don’t want to talk about it, whatever. But don’t sit there and tell me I’m imagining things.”

“Even if you are?”

“Okay now you’re just pissing me off, Jane. Goodbye.”

Jane glares at her phone in annoyance. She shuts off the display, slips it into her purse and continues driving to her apartment.

***

Monday morning, Babe’s mother Caroline is behind the wheel of her SUV. It’s a significant step up from the old red pickup that Babe shares with her brother. Early morning sun shines through the windshield onto Caroline. Country music plays at a low volume in the SUV.

Trip and Babe are sitting together in the backseat. His shoulder bag is on the floor by his feet. Babe’s luggage is stowed in the back end of the truck.

Caroline looks at Trip in the rearview mirror. “We got a while before we get to the bus station. I’d love to hear some more of your stories, Trip.”

“Okay. Well,” he turns to Babe, “there is something I wanted to run by you.”

“What’s that?”

“It’s a standing vacation I take every fall, and I’d like to bring you this year. If you’re interested.”

“I’m sure I will be. Where to?”

“Italy.”

“Italy?” Babe’s hands fly over her mouth.

“Wow.” In the front seat, Caroline’s face brightens with intrigue.

Babe lowers her hands to her lap, fidgeting with the hem of her shorts. “Gosh, I ain’t never been on a plane before.”

Trip peers at her rattled reaction. “Is that why you wanted to take the bus? Are you scared to fly?”

“Um, I–”

Caroline chimes in. “I’ll go.”

“Mama!” She bellows, ruffled by her mother’s offer.

“Calm down, I’m only jokin’.” Caroline winks at Trip in the rearview mirror. “Tell us about this vacation you take.”

“It’s a hobby my stepdad passed onto me while I was living out there. I go out there every fall to follow up with the tradition.”

“Well, what is it?” Babe asks him.

“Have you heard of truffles?”

“Like a chocolate truffle?”

“No. A truffle, like a mushroom.”

“A mushroom?” She scrunches her nose.

“Yes, a mushroom.” Trip smiles at her. “Every year, a particular kind called a white diamond comes up. So, Giancarlo would always take me up to this one spot in Northern Italy and we’d hunt them with Charlie.”

“Who?” Babe is lost. “Who’s Charlie?”

“The dog. He was half Bloodhound and half Basset Bleu, so he had this really cool, brindled orange coat. Man, he could hang in there.” Trip fondly reminisces. “He never ran out of steam, and he was pretty small, so he could get into some tight spots up on those hills. Anyway, this dog was professionally trained to hunt these white truffles.”

Babe shakes her head. Up in the front seat, Caroline is shaking her head in unison with Babe who says,

“Wow, the things you folks don’t spend good dollars on.”

“Amen.” Caroline agrees.

“Sometimes you have to spend a little to make a little. These mushrooms go for a lot of money per pound on the market.”

“What market?” Babe snickers at him. “The truffle market?”

“Yes.”

This newsflash silences Babe for a moment. “You’re tellin’ me these funguses are so special that people not only train animals to find them, but spend thousands of dollars to eat them?”

“Mostly restaurants will buy them in bulk and serve them.”

“That just blows my mind. I ain’t a fan of fungus, but I gotta see one of these for myself.”

“The trip is really more for the experience than the tuber.”

“The wha...?”

“The truffle,” he rephrases, “even though some people claim they’re an aphrodisiac. My friend Random has me bring some back for him. He makes them into oil, actually.”

“Is that so?”

“It is.” Trip nods.

Befuddlement washes over Babe. “Was I hearin’ you wrong, or did you just say you have a friend named Random?”

***

“Out of the new people around here, I think you’re gonna end up liking Shay.” Random’s comment comes out of Sam’s phone speaker, lying on the rug next to her. She is on the bedroom floor in her Amsterdam flat, sitting across from a black bookshelf.

“Yeah, I’ve heard that from others.” She skims the bookshelf, which is divided into sections of different-sized shelving. It’s primarily filled with rows upon rows of CDs, along with some vinyl and other music-related items. There’s a plastic tub on the floor beside Sam. She reaches up for a handful of CDs.

“She sort of does what you used to do here,” Random tells her.

Sam lurches from confusion to outright offense. “Shay runs the house?” She holds the handful of CDs out in front of her.

“No, she’s member relations.” He stifles a laugh.

“That’s what I thought.” Instantly calmer, Sam puts the CDs into the plastic tub beside her. “That’s not what I used to do.”

“I know that. I’m just saying she’s good with the members, like you were.”

“Okay, so then what am I going to do when I get back there?” Sam reaches into the bookshelf for more CDs.

“What do you think? Run the house with me.”

“Huh.” She puts the CDs into the bubble-wrap lined tub with care.

“Why do you sound surprised?”

“I guess I thought you had that under control.” Sam rests her arm across the top of the tub.

“I do.”

“But you don’t have any other jobs in mind for me?”

“No. I’m just looking forward to having you back. I haven’t been thinking up ways that I can put you to work around here,” he says with a chuckle.

“You know how I need projects, though.” Sam shrugs. “I can always do scenarios.”

“Or not.”

“What? Why do you say that?”

“You could plan them.”

“I can do them, too. Used to do ‘em all the time.” She contends and goes for more CDs in the bookshelf.

“I don’t really envision you out in the field, honestly.”

“Why not?”

“The actual scenes are pretty well staffed these days. But you could always work on the back end, you know? Help plan them out.”

“At first, maybe.” Sam disputes him, dead set on getting back out into the field.

“I think you’re jumping ahead of yourself, Sam. Just work on getting your ass here. I think everything will fall into place once you’re back.”

“I’m sure.” She tucks another row of CDs into the tub. Across from her, one shelf is entirely cleared.

“So, what are you doing tonight?”

“I’m packing up my music collection. I think I can survive a few weeks without it.”

“I’ll protect it for you when it arrives.” He offers her.

“Yes!” She blurts with sudden persistence, having made the mistake of telling Black her stuff would arrive in California before she does. “Please keep my things under lock and key when they get there.”

“Yeah, especially since somebody’s decided to lighten up his schedule, as of late.” Random gibes critically.

“What are you referring to?”

***

At Becky’s townhouse, mid-morning sun comes through her glass patio door and fills her dining room with light. Her new phone is on the table next to the Submission book. The bookmark is tucked in all the way to the back cover.

She strides out of the adjacent kitchen with a steaming mug of coffee. She is fresh faced and dressed for the day in a cute white blouse, apple green jacket and black capris. She sits down at the dining room table and picks up her phone.

Despite her uphill battle with Black, Becky appears sunny and optimistic. She calls Black and holds the phone to her ear, waiting for the beep of his voicemail. She leaves him a cordial message. “Hello. I totally get that you don’t want to talk to me, and I also hope it’s temporary. Because I really do acknowledge that I screwed up. And I know that night was bad, but I don’t think it’s all been bad.” She stops to sip her coffee. “Anyway, I’ve been running a lot of things through my head lately. I’m starting to understand where I went wrong, and how I perceived you wrong. And I’m still working on it, so I hope on some level that matters to you. Or maybe it will after a while when you’re not as angry with me. Thank you for listening.” Becky ends the call on an upbeat note and sets her phone on the table.

***

Later that same night in Amsterdam, Sam is sitting up in bed with her phone to her ear. The Velvet Underground picture hangs on the wall above her head. On the wall across from her bed is a computer desk with a large monitor and keyboard. The monitor is off. The black bookshelf on the side of the room is emptied and packed away.

“So, tell me something,” Sam says to her best friend on the phone...

“What?” Rayne is floating on a foam raft in the Mercer Estate pool. She’s the only one in the pool, given that it’s still fairly early in the day.

“Why would Random not want me to do scenarios?” Sam asks her.

Rayne casts her emerald eyes over the water in consideration. “I can think of a few reasons, but it’s probably because we had a situation a while back where a target recognized one of us.”

“I remember hearing about that.” Sam recollects the incident. “It was that Reno guy who got identified.”

“Ever since then, if you’re a main player in scenarios here, you’re encouraged to lie low during the weekends.”

“So then, no parties?”

“Parties and beyond, but yeah, mainly that.” Rayne verifies the new regulation.

“Okay, I guess that makes sense. I don’t know why he couldn’t have just said that, instead of making it seem like he was telling me what I could or could not do.”

“To read your reaction.”

“You’re probably right. God, you’re so damn sharp.”

Rayne takes her compliment modestly. “You’re just out of practice.”

“No, you have always been my beacon of common sense.”

“My ego will adore having you back here, dearest.” Rayne looks up at Hannah strutting across the pool area. Hannah is wrapped in the fluffy white towel that Will delivers to her every morning. She’s holding her daily glass of orange juice and banana.

Hannah waves at Rayne on her way to the hot tub. When she approaches the sunken tub, Black and Cade are already inside.

Black’s phone is lying on the side of the tub, on speaker, playing that morning’s voicemail from Becky. “I’m starting to understand where I went wrong, and how I perceived you wrong. And I’m still working on it, so I hope on some level that matters to you.”

When Black sees Hannah, he reaches over to pause the message.

“Don’t stop on my account.” She sets down her breakfast and removes her towel.

“Good morning.” Cade discreetly watches Hannah step into the hot tub.

“What’s going on, Black?” Hannah ducks down in the warm water and scoots into her spot. “Are you dropping this new recruit, or what?”

“I don’t know yet.”

“He’s having cold feet.” Cade insinuates.

“It’s not cold feet.” Black contests him.

“It’s impatience.” Hannah turns to Black.

“No.”

“Then, you’re expecting it to go like a typical sub recruit. But it isn’t. Any self-respecting Top is bound to have an intrinsic dominant streak. Don’t hold that against her.”

Black eloquently retorts. “In order to learn something inside and out, you have to experience what you want to attain. Then when you evolve to Dominant, you can fully relate to the sub state of mind. And I think that makes you better at it.”

“Uh-huh.” Hannah shoots him a skeptical reply. “I’m obviously aware of that school of thought, but I’ve never bought into it. Not that there’s anything wrong with it.” She swings her hand up in amity. “But I believe you are what you are. There is no switching. There is no need to be a sub before you become a Dom, in my opinion.”

“Well I do buy into that school of thought.”

“I know you do.” She sways in towards Black. “And Becky’s your project. And if she wants it badly enough, she’ll do what you ask.” Hannah sways back. “But don’t expect her to make it easy for you. She’s not a sub.”

***

Becky opens the door to Exotica tattoo parlor and walks inside, breezing past the colorful decals plastered on the stucco walls. A hint of patchouli incense hovers in the air. Becky spots a familiar employee, the bald white woman with a silver nose ring, standing near the beaded curtain.

“Can I help you?”

“Is Alice available?” Becky accosts her.

“Yeah.” The employee draws the beaded curtain open as she calls down the hallway. “Hey Alice!” She turns back around. “Go ahead.” She holds the beaded curtain for Becky, who steps through the doorway.

“Thanks.” Becky goes down the hallway and stops in front of Alice’s studio door. Alternative rock music thumps inside.

Alice is waiting on the other side of the doorway with a glimmer of recognition. “I remember you. Come in.” She spins away from Becky. Her hair hangs down her back in little braids. Her tattooed arms are covered up with a plaid flannel shirt. Alice heads for her black padded tattoo chair. She genially runs her hand across the headrest. “Have a seat.” Alice walks over to the counter along the wall and sits on one of the wood stools. She picks up a small remote to turn down the music. Alice pulls her bare feet up and sits cross-legged on the stool.

“Thank you.” Becky relaxes into the black tattoo chair, resting her arms comfortably across her stomach. “And thanks for talking to me.”

“Sure thing.” Alice has a laidback aura. Her attention shifts down to Becky’s crotch. “Is it about your ring?”

“No.” Becky slides her legs closer together and makes eye contact with Alice. “It’s actually about the guy who I met in here last week, and the whole...” Becky lifts her hand in an effort to ascertain the appropriate label.

“Collective?”

“Is that the right word, collective?”

“It’s fitting.” Alice shrugs at her.

“Okay, then.” Becky lowers her hand back down to her stomach. “Can you tell me how you’re involved?”

“I’m an outer member.” Alice speaks in a demure key, like she’s choosing her words carefully. “Do you know what that is?”

“No.” Becky responds bluntly.

Alice twirls one of her braids around her finger. “Hmm.” She clues Becky in. “Well, I don’t live there, at the house.”

“You mean like Black and,” Becky points down at the chair she’s sitting on, “this guy, from the other day?”

“Yes.”

“And since they do live there, they’re inner party, right?”

“That’s right.”

“How well do you know Black?”

A covert smile spreads across Alice’s face. “We’ve crossed paths a few times.”

“Oh.” Becky quells the disappointment in her voice. “So you’re like, involved with him?”

Alice’s eyes bug out. “No.” She shakes her head vigorously. “No. Not what you’re thinking. I have no ties to Black. He’s just, tied me up a few times, you know?” She touches her fingers to her chest. “At the request of my Dom.” Alice clarifies before resting her arm on the counter beside her.

“Mm-hmm.” Becky drops her head back onto the headrest and drums her fingers on her abdomen. “So you’re a sub.”

“Correct.”

“Do you happen to know what ‘random’ means, on the phone?” Becky asks.

“Random is actually the nickname of the guy who heads up the collective. He had the network set up for the phones.”

“I see.” She lifts her head from the headrest. “How long have you been involved with this collective?”

“A few years.”

Becky looks at Alice with a serious expression. “Can you tell me where the house is?”

“Sorry.” Alice flatly refuses.

“I figured that was a longshot.”

***

The cabin of the bus is lined with pairs of royal blue, highbacked seats that face one another. Babe is between the seats, bending down to slide disposable coffee cups into the cup holders. She overhears people murmuring in the seats behind her. Babe peeks over and greets the passengers in the next row back.

Right past that row of seats is the bus bathroom. The handle of the door is spun to ‘occupied’...

Locked inside of the bus bathroom, Trip sits on the toilet seat lid. He flicks the lighter in his hand and raises the spoon, where a hit of heroin is floating in some water. Trip gradually heats the spoon, tipping it a little to mix the contents. A couple of bubbles form in the spoon...

While Trip’s busy in the bathroom, Babe is knelt on her seat, hanging over the back and chattering to the people in the row behind her. It’s a mother traveling with her six-year-old daughter.

“You’re headin’ to Phoenix? Phoenix is our transfer.” Babe glimpses over and sees Trip coming down the aisle towards her. She turns back to the woman. “You two enjoy the rest of your ride, then.” Babe beams at them and twists around. She glides down into her seat.

Trip sits across from her. He runs his palms down the armrests of the plush blue seats and glances out the window, exceedingly tranquil. Across from him, Babe scoots out to the edge of her seat. She bows into him.

“Hi.”

He smiles down at her. “Hi.”

“Feelin’ better?”

“Much.” Trip asserts. “I’m so glad I go with my instincts, because they were right again.”

“About?”

“About you.”

“Oh.” She reaches for Trip’s armrest and clasps his hand. “That’s just what I was thinkin’. I see you, Trip. For what you are, I mean. And I think I see you because on the inside, I’m just like you.”

“That would be a really fortunate thing if it’s true.”

“It is.” Babe persists.

“There’s just so much you haven’t seen yet.” He strokes her cheek. “I’m kind of worried you might feel out of place at first.”

“But, as long as you’re there.”

“Of course I’ll be there.”

“Trust me, I know I’m gettin’ in a little over my head, and this is all pretty spontaneous for a girl like me.” Babe moves over into the seat next to Trip. She cozies up to him and starts to express how completely open she is about what lies ahead. “You live life like the squirrel, you know? Just for the sport of it. I get that about you. I want that too, and I got nothin’ to lose. You saw what my life was like.”

“There’s nothing wrong with your life.”

“But I want you to show me how to be a squirrel, too.”

All Trip can seem to do is smile at her uncontaminated quirkiness. Babe is a true-blue novelty. “Ah, how are you even possible?” He wraps his arm around her shoulders and pulls her in close. He drops a light kiss on the side of Babe’s head.

“What do you mean?”

“How is such a perfect person even possible?”

“Oh, please. I didn’t even know what a truffle was, Trip. Remember that?”

“Yes.”

“I’m not cultured at all.” Babe lowers her volume. “And I know the girls you must date in California...”

Trip leans back and corrects Babe. “I don’t date any girls in California, so don’t worry about that. You’re exactly what I need.”

“With time, I’ll bore you.”

Trip submits to Babe’s transparent request for reassurance. “No, not a chance.”

***

That afternoon, Cade is behind the wheel of his black SUV, braking at a stoplight. Alone in the truck, he picks up his phone to double-check Jane’s location on the GPS map. He sees that she just arrived at the Community Health Center, presumably for class, which will occupy her for a while.

He shuts off the display and tosses his phone down on the passenger seat. The light turns green, so he proceeds through it and steers into the parking lot of a high-end apartment complex.

Near the entrance of the complex is a cluster box mailbox, surrounded by an elegantly landscaped flower garden. Cade parks right in front of the cluster box. He gets out of his truck and walks up to it.

With the white envelope for Jane in his hand, Cade scans the mailboxes. He finds Jane’s box and slides the envelope into her slot.

Cade gets back into his truck, puts it in reverse and backs away from the cluster box. He navigates out of the apartment complex before reaching for his phone to call Shay.

“Hello Cade,” she says on the other line. “What’s going on?”

“Is chamber six still available tomorrow night?”

“Hang on... Yeah, it is.” She confirms.

“Can you reserve it for me?”

“Sure. Where are you, anyway? You know the meeting starts in like thirty minutes.”

“I’ll make it back.”

***

Sunlight shines onto the plants filling the windowsill in the contemporary therapist’s office where Becky has a 1:30 p.m. appointment. She sits stiffly on the cream-colored couch across from the therapist. Across the room, the essential oil diffuser emits a lavender mist. Becky is obviously sheepish about being back, but she’s there to unload on an unbiased set of ears.

“That’s a cute jacket.” The therapist kicks things off on a light note.

“Thanks.” Becky brushes her hand down the sleeve of her apple green jacket. “I really didn’t want to come back here.”

“I got that impression. What happened?” The homely therapist crosses her leg and rests her notepad on her knee.

“Do you remember the guy I was dating at the time?”

“I do.” She revisits her notes. “Brian.”

“Yeah, Brian dumped me the following day, believe it or not. Then he went missing later that week and hasn’t resurfaced.”

“Hmm.” Openly curious, the therapist begins writing on her notepad as Becky continues.

“So then I went and met this other guy I’d been talking to online for a few months, and I managed to drive him off too, by mistake.” A blaze of determination simmers in her eyes. She slants forward in her seat. “Except unlike Brian, I can’t let this one go.”

The therapist glances up from her notepad at Becky. “Sounds like you’re serious about him.” She resumes taking notes.

“But I don’t even know if it’s mutual. And it’s pretty stupid of me to even care this much. Because he’s really– he’s really just an illusion.” Becky huffs. “But, stupid me is drawn to this illusion for some reason. And next thing you know, I’m quitting my job to free up my schedule for him. Who does that?”

“You quit your job?”

Becky nods at the therapist, who has not stopped scribbling notes.

“How well do you know this new guy?”

“I know him, but, not in the ways you usually get to know people.” Becky attempts an explanation.

“Sounds complex.”

“It is complex.”

The therapist stops writing and lowers her pen. She focuses on Becky across the coffee table. “What is his appeal?”

“It’s just how remarkably different he is from anyone else I’ve ever been involved with.”

“Different is really powerful stuff for somebody who’s in a funk.”

“Exactly.” Becky agrees. “It’s like a project, trying to understand him and what he does. And at the same time, it’s hugely charming to have somebody paying attention to me like that, too.”

“Hmm.” The therapist taps her pen on her notepad.

“So,” Becky presses on in a petitioning tone, “do you have any advice? I know that you’re not really supposed to give advice, but I’m asking you.”

“Well Becky, it sounds to me like you’re going through an early mid-life crisis.”

Becky cocks her head, giving credence to the therapist’s observation.

“That’s a starting point.”

“A starting point for what?” Becky blinks at her in uncertainty.

“Doesn’t that clarity make you see your situation any differently?”

“No. Putting a label on a feeling doesn’t take away the feeling.”

***

Later that night, Cade, Shay and Black are sitting in Adirondack chairs around the crackling fire pit in the Mercer Estate pool area. Cade is occupied with his phone. Shay has a laptop on her thighs.

Black is drinking a cup of coffee. “When’s Trip getting back?” he asks Shay.

“Sometime Wednesday.”

“Wednesday?” He sets his coffee mug on the arm of his chair. “I’m surprised that wasn’t mentioned at the meeting today.”

“The details surrounding the Trip situation are still a bit murky at this point, but I do know one interesting thing.” Shay looks up from her computer screen at him. “He’s bringing back a souvenir from Oklahoma.”

“A flesh and blood souvenir?” Black infers, smirking at her.

“Yup.”

“He really has a weak spot for the southern belles,” Cade says and chuckles.

“Seems so.” Shay concurs with him. “Anyway, it may or may not be a short-lived situation.”

“Depending on what she thinks when she gets here?”

“Yeah.” She puffs out a short laugh at Cade. “He literally plucked this girl straight off the farm, so we’ll see what happens.”

***

At that same time, Becky is inside of Trudy’s tavern, crossing through the noisy, green-lit nightclub. Once again, the therapist didn’t provide Becky with any new information or insight, so she’s back to figuring things out in her own way.

An obnoxious punk rock tune pumps through the club. Becky spots the tall cocktail table along the wall, near the small dance area. It’s the same one she sat at with Black when they were there. The tall table is available since the club is only about half full. She roams over to it and takes a seat.

The well-endowed brunette cocktail waitress steps up to her table sporting a lime green bikini top. “What are you having?”

Becky looks up at her face. “Rum and cola, please.”

“Sure.” The waitress makes her way to the bar.

Becky sets her purse on the table and begins perusing the club. The dance floor beside her is empty. Across the room, she sees a blonde sitting on one of the black couches. Becky leans in over the table for a closer look. It’s not Molly (Shay). She slumps back in her barstool and keeps on searching, but she doesn’t recognize anyone in the club.

***

Back at the fire pit, Shay sits upright in her Adirondack chair and homes in on her computer screen enthusiastically, like she’s ready to get down to business with Cade and Black. “All right, I’d like to rehash the Monday meeting stuff with you guys.”

Cade sets his phone on the arm of the chair. “Let’s do it.” He gives Shay his undivided attention.

“You got tasked with organizing the party this week, didn’t you?” Black recalls. He’s lazily sprawled out in his chair next to Shay, who starts prattling.

“The theme for Saturday is gonna be a Bourbon Street masquerade ball with our trademark dark twist on it, of course.” She trails down the to-do list on her screen. “My suite can get a lot of this stuff together, honestly.”

“Have them get in touch with mine.” Cade offers his subordinates’ help.

Black picks up his coffee. “Send me a copy of the menu for Kaime,” he tells Shay.

“Okay.” Her fingers move across the keyboard. “Now the performance is going to be suspension, so we’ll need to get the technical things coordinated throughout the week, here.”

“Are there any ideas for that, yet?” Cade hunches forward in his chair with piqued interest.

Focused on her screen, Shay tips her head. “Not really.” Her gaze drifts up. “I was just picturing a few hook stands around the room.” She studies Cade. “Why? Do you want to take it over?”

“Yeah, I’ll handle that.”

“Cool.” Outwardly relieved, Shay wafts back down to her laptop. “I will assign the performance to you, then.” She transfers the item off of her own to-do list.

***

Becky walks out of Trudy’s tavern and pulls her new phone out of her purse. She calls Black, skimming over the parked cars in the lot while she waits for his voicemail. “So, I’m actually standing in the parking lot where things went to hell with you. I was thinking back on that night, and I remembered when I originally asked you if you knew the two women on the leather couches. And I realized that you never denied knowing them. Why didn’t I pick up on that? Why wasn’t I paying attention?” She paces around the parking lot. “No wonder you got so frustrated when I wanted to sort things out with Molly, because I should’ve figured out the trick on my own. I mean, I guessed right off the bat that you knew them. It was so stupid of me to keep pushing the issue, and I get that now.” Becky hears the door of the club open behind her. Over her shoulder, she sees an older guy moseying out to his car in the parking lot.

Becky gets back to leaving her message. “Anyway, I know you probably hate me rambling like this, but I don’t want to just apologize without letting you know that I actually understand what I’m apologizing for. I’ve been retracing my steps, trying to see what I might’ve missed.” She pauses and humbly stares up at the night sky. “And I’ve also been hoping to run into you, let’s face it.”

***

Back at the fire pit, Black has his phone up to his ear. The tail end of Becky’s message plays out on his phone. “Anyway, I’m sure that sounds desperate, and I guess I am. But I just can’t give up on this.”

Contemplative, Black deletes the message and sets his phone down on the arm of his chair. “Hmm.”

“What?” Shay peers over at him.

“She really seems to be trying.”

“Who, Becky?”

Black nods at Shay.

“Have you ignored her for a week, yet?”

“Just about.”

“Then it’s just about time to get back to that. Deal with her, you know?”

“I do know.” Black assents. Shay gets back to the to-do list on her laptop.

On the other side of Shay, Cade is absorbed into the GPS map displayed on his phone screen. “Jane just got to her apartment.”

“Spare us the play-by-play, Cade.” Shay quips.

“Sorry.”

Black finishes off the last drink of his coffee. He glances around at the empty Adirondack chairs circling the fire pit before landing on Shay. “How’d Reno get out of this supplemental meeting tonight, by the way?”

“He’s doing a scenario tomorrow.”

“So am I,” Black looks over at Cade, “for charity.”

“That doesn’t really count then, does it?” Shay differentiates and also looks over at Cade, who’s zooming the map on his screen to determine Jane’s precise location.

***

Alone in her car, Jane drives up to the cluster box mailbox that’s tucked into the flourishing flower garden. The mailbox area is lit by a streetlamp. Jane gets out of the car and walks over to unlock her box. She takes out a stack of mail. Jane carries the mail over to her car and gets back inside.

While sorting through random bills and solicitations, she catches sight of a white envelope. Only her first name is written on the envelope. The handwriting is similar to the envelope left in her car previously.

Jane tosses the rest of her mail onto the passenger seat and opens the white envelope. She pulls out a card. The card has the scales of justice on the front of it. She flips open the card and devours the message inside:

Jane, I hear you want to meet me. We can arrange that for tomorrow night. But in order for that to happen, here’s what I need you to do...

As she reads the card, she recoils in terror.

Chapter 3

The next morning, Rayne holds up an expensive camera and aims it at a tired-eyed, albeit attractive guy in his forties with a nice build. Ted looks into the camera lens, and the flash goes off.

“Thank you,” she says to him.

“No problem.”

They’re inside the main office, which is located on the Mercer Estate’s ground floor. Rayne turns around to set the camera on a floating shelf behind her. She exits the office, and Shay walks in. The heels of Shay’s boots click on the slate-colored tile below.

“Hello, Ted?” Shay stands across from him, extending her hand.

“Yes, nice to meet you.” They shake hands.

“I’m Shay.”

“Shay Fontaine. Member relations.”

She nods at him and gestures to a pair of high back leather armchairs. “Have a seat.” She heads to the desk chairs on the opposite side of a spacious, glossy desk where Random is already sat. Shay sits down beside Random, who is reviewing the contents of a file folder. She addresses Ted across the desk. “Who referred you to us?”

“A client of mine did, actually.”

“That must’ve been an interesting conversation.” Random closes the folder and hands it over to Shay. Morning sun shines in through the picture window behind them. A still metronome sits on the windowsill.

“Sometimes in my business, you get to know your clients pretty well.”

Shay opens the file folder and lays it on the desk. “You’re a contractor.”

“Yes.”

“Commercial or residential?”

“Residential. Primarily custom homes and remodels.”

“How did this subject come up with your client?” Random signals to Ted’s application in the file in front of Shay.

“Well, it stemmed from a joke about building a secret room in his house, a dungeon.”

Shay peeks up from the file with a smile on her face. “Did you build the secret room?”

“No. Not yet, anyway.” Ted smiles back at her.

Aside from the floating shelf by the doorway and the large desk sandwiched by posh chairs, the only other piece of furniture in the office is a bookcase on the wall across from the door. Clean, classy and minimalist, it’s an open canvas for the diverse array that enters here with a myriad of motives. Most member-related business is handled in the main office, particularly applications and renewals.

“Considering that you have no experience with the lifestyle, what exactly makes you want to fork over the membership fee to join us?” Random probes him.

“I really need an outlet.” Ted sums it up. “I’ve been working sixteen-hour days for the past eight months and I need an escape pretty bad.” He looks out the picture window at the pristine front lawn. “I had to cancel an appointment just to make it over here for this.” He relays to Random. “I heard this is the place to be on Saturday nights. That’s what I need.”

“You’re in it for the recreational aspect, then?”

“A weekend getaway,” Ted tells him. “At first, anyway. Once I’ve had a chance to decompress, maybe it’ll develop into more.”

“It’s not a bad little weekend retreat.” Random attests.

“So I hear. How hard is it to get a guest room here on Saturday nights?”

“You can either pay upfront for a guaranteed, regular room or you can take your chances.” Random gives him the two available options.

“I might have to look into that.” Ted debates while Shay pounces on a different line of questioning.

“How many houses under construction do you have going right now?”

“Three. One of them is almost complete.”

“Hmm.” She swaps a scheming glance with Random. “Are you familiar with our scenario service, Ted?”

“I am, actually.”

“I have one coming up that calls for a dark and impersonal, semi-public location. And I think a house under construction at night fits the bill.”

“No wonder you got me in for an appointment so quickly.” Ted chuckles at her.

Shay makes no effort to conceal her ulterior motive. “It can be mutually beneficial.”

“I’m listening.”

“Given the situation we’re in, we could just deduct your compensation off of the fee, today.” Random handles the negotiation. “Or maybe work out a trade deal.”

Ted arches his brows in accord. “I can do that. What kind of trade?”

“You seemed interested in the guest rooms.”

“I am. Could I get a guaranteed room for a year?”

Random politely denies his bid. “No, I don’t have nearly enough in it for that.”

“Okay. What can you do, then?”
