Cade lets out a short laugh on his way up to the dresser. He picks up a lighter to light the row of vanilla pillar candles in the middle of the dresser, a comfortable scent to soften the prominent aroma of leather in the chamber.

Reno polishes off his meal and tosses his trash into the empty sack. “That stuff you wanted is in your office, by the way.”

“The cable wire and turnbuckle hook?” Cade finishes lighting the candles and goes over to the chamber door.

“Yeah, what’s that for, anyway?”

The sting of Cade’s smack brought a little tear to Jane’s eyes, blurring her vision even further. The industrial white noise throbs in her ears as she blinks the tear away and regains her focus. She sees a figure pass by in front of her. The figure stops near the door.

Cade is standing by the chamber door, reaching for the dimmer switch.

“Wow, fancy. But how’re you gonna get her up there?” Reno asks him.

“A crank, a pulley-system, you know?”

“Sure, I guess that would work.”

“Are you done eating?”

“Yeah.”

Cade spins the switch, dimming the lights almost completely down.

The figure’s outline gradually fades into the darkness around it. Jane leans forward and squints, but she’s lost sight of the person moving through the room. Her vision is all but gone, so she closes her eyes and tugs against her restraints until she’s distracted by the feeling of warmth encircling her bare ankle.

Cade grabs onto one of Jane’s ankles. “Help me get her onto the bench, and I think that’s all I need from you.”

“Okay.”

***

“Oh m’gosh, I ate too much.” On the bus, Babe settles into the plush blue seat with a groan. Trip sits down next to her. A couple of blankets and pillows are neatly piled on the seats across from them.

The vacuum-like sound of the bus door is heard, and a nearby passenger takes their seat.

“Well, I don’t think we have another meal stop until early tomorrow morning.” Trip gets his phone out of his pocket and brings up the rest of their itinerary. “So that should tide you over.”

“And then some.” She yawns. “I’m ready for some sleep.” Babe closes the window covering. She peers up at the overhead lights.

Trip glances over at her. “I’m sure they’ll turn off the lights when we start moving again.” He scrolls down the screen of his phone and laughs under his breath.

“What?” Babe glimpses over at Trip’s phone.

“No, I was just thinking about something.”

“What?”

“It’s nothing.” He shrugs off her question.

“What?” she asks again even louder.

“Hey, shhh.” Trip shushes her with a scowl.

“Sorry.” Babe starts whispering. “What were you thinkin’ about?” She reaches for one of the lightweight blankets in the seat across from her. “Be honest, now.” She unfolds the blanket.

“Okay.” Trip sets his phone down on his knee. “Earlier, I was gonna ask you if you packed your uniform.”

“You mean my school uniform, right?” Babe drapes the blanket over her body.

“Yes. And just now, I was thinking about how I’m glad I didn’t ask you that.”

“Why? Cause I packed it.”

He looks down at her. “You did?”

Babe looks back up at him. “Yeah.” She kicks her shoes off onto the floor. “You sounded interested in seein’ it.”

“Well, that was before I knew.” Trip slips his phone into his pocket.

“Knew what?”

“Before I knew that you were still chaste.” He spells it out.

“Oh...oh.” Babe gets it. She draws the blanket up under her chin. “I guess I didn’t know that’d be such a big thing.”

***

Later that night in chamber 6, Cade bends down to pull the headphones off of Jane. Even though the scene was centered on her, Cade smiles, equally sated. He takes the headphones across the room and sets them on the shelf by the door. In the corner of the shelf is a change of clothes and bottle of water for her.

Jane is lying on her stomach on the weightlifting bench. Her head hangs over the front end of it. Damp strands of hair are stuck to the back of Jane’s sweaty neck. The scarf is still over her eyes, but the gag is no longer in her mouth. Jane’s knees are bent, and her arms are at her sides. Her wrists are bound to her ankles down below.

Cade turns the lights back up and walks over to the weight bench. Jane lifts her blindfolded head up. He crouches down in front of her, nose to nose.

“Hi,” she says.

“Hi.” Cade reaches for Jane’s temples. He slides the scarf up over her forehead and buries his fingers in Jane’s hair, holding her head in his hands. The scarf drops to the floor.

When Jane looks into Cade’s calm brown eyes, she blushes, overwhelmed with pure emotion. Her face crunches up in tears.

“Stop it.” He pulls Jane’s face into his and kisses her forehead. “It’s okay.” He assures her. Cade sweeps his thumbs under Jane’s lashes to wipe away her tears. He tilts her face up towards his.

***

Parked in the driveway of the house under construction, Kayleigh sits behind the wheel of Cade’s SUV. A nearby streetlamp casts a white glow on the black truck. The lot on one side of the house is for sale, and the lot on the other side is just a foundation.

Nick and Brian come out the front door of the house carrying black trash bags. Brian pushes the door shut, and Nick locks it up. He has a duffel bag over his shoulder.

From inside the truck, Kayleigh pops open the back door for them. The interior lights come on, and psychedelic rock music spills out the back door. Nick and Brian arrive at the back of the truck to load up the trash bags.

“Wow.” Kayleigh lauds over her shoulder at them, highly impressed. “That was quick.” She bumps down the music volume.

“That was one of the easiest cleanups I think I’ve ever done.” Nick closes the back door. He gets into the passenger side of the truck, and Brian gets into the seat behind him.

Kayleigh starts the engine and backs out of the driveway.

“Brian, this is Kayleigh.” Nick introduces them.

“Hello.” Kayleigh checks out Brian’s reflection in the rearview mirror.

“I’ve seen you around. How’s it going?”

“Not too bad. I’m ready for that.” She refers to the inconspicuous joint sitting in the front console.

“Me too.” Nick picks up the joint and rifles around in his pocket for a lighter.

“There’s one right here.” Kayleigh taps the cupholder. “Thanks again for sitting through dinner tonight, Nick.”

“So, what was the deal with your brother’s girlfriend, by the way?” Nick lights the joint and takes a couple big puffs.

“Madison.” Kayleigh grips the steering wheel in exasperation. “That girl has to be the center of attention ALL the time. She is like, the worst kind of idiot. My brother could do so much better.” She takes the joint from Nick and holds it between her fingers like a cigarette.

“Where’d you guys go to dinner?” Brian asks her from the backseat.

“Oh, it was this seafood place on the beach. I don’t even remember the name of it.”

“Something-wharf.” That’s all Nick can come up with. “It was good food, but–” He’s interrupted by a ringing phone.

“That’s me.” Kayleigh pulls her phone out of her purse. “It’s Black.” She announces before answering the call. “Hello.”

“Where are you at?” he asks on the other line.

“Picking up Nick from Reno’s job.”

“How’d everything go?”

“Fine, as far as I know. Are you checking up on me?” she asks playfully.

“No, I’m killing time,” Black tells her.

“That sounds more like you. Killing time before what?”

***

Later that night, Jane is in the passenger seat of Black’s Mercedes. She’s wearing an Eraserhead t-shirt over her short black skirt. She screws the cap back onto the bottle of water she’s holding. A light indie rock song strums through the car.

“How come he sent me away so soon?” Jane asks Black, who’s behind the wheel. He’s giving her a ride home.

“Probably because it’s late,” he hypothesizes, “trying not to interfere with the rest of your life.”

“I wouldn’t have minded the interference.”

Streetlights brighten the sides of the highway. Traffic is sparse.

“So,” Black begins speaking to her nonchalantly, “is it safe to assume that you’ve refrained?”

“Refrained?” Jane clearly isn’t making the connection. Her eyes are still glazed over with the afterglow of meeting Cade.

“From other physical contact.”

“OH, yeah, yes.” She confirms that she has not been with any other men.

“Privately?”

“Privately? No.” She confides through a reserved laugh.

“So, you’ve cheated?”

Jane doesn’t respond, inwardly wrestling with the idea of discussing her masturbatory life. “How is that cheating?”

“I mean you cheated in the game. It’s cheating yourself, is what it is.”

“Then, technically I guess I have.”

“You’ll need to stop that.”

“Really?” she asks, startled by his statement. “That’s expanding the boundaries of ‘the game’ pretty far, isn’t it?”

“No it isn’t. It’s a compromise.” Black explains evenly. “Keeping your hands off of yourself is for your own good, anyway. There’s no physical benefit for him. It’s entirely mental, for you.”

“Sure.” Jane nods in understanding.

“And giving control over that one aspect of your life isn’t really that different from any relationship.”

“That’s true.”

“So just trust it and go with it.”

“It’s a little difficult to trust someone I know so little about.” She speaks rationally in an effort to conceal her open willingness to give Cade that control.

“You know more than you think. Most people don’t give you the truth first.”

“Or so you say. I don’t mean to be disrespectful, or anything.”

“No, I know what you’re getting at.” To Black, Jane’s defensive responses are typical, predictable. “It’s only natural to rely on logic and past experience. And I know that you don’t have anything else tangible to compare this situation to, but you can’t make that your argument for distrust.”

Jane digests his narrative. “You’re right.” She agrees. “I’m just not used to this.”

“If you were used to shit like this, I don’t think we’d need to be having this conversation right now,” he says.

“No, probably not.” She smiles at him.

They slow down to a stop at a red light. Black reaches into his pocket for Jane’s keys. “Here.” He hands them over to her. “Given the unusual circumstances, you’ve been well taken care of.”

“Yes, I know.” Jane lowers the keys to her lap. “I’m pretty impressed with him.” She has a faraway look on her face. “I guess I’m just used to people having an ulterior motive.”

“Then you’ll need to train yourself to see Cade in a new light.”

“That would be easier to do if I understood what was in it for him,” she says bluntly.

“What?” Black shoots her a perplexed frown. “Isn’t that obvious?”

“Um, no. He hasn’t exactly been sexually gratified, himself.”

“Well, he’s not a rapist.” Black retorts in a matter of fact. The light turns green, and he takes a right at the intersection. “This game can be effectively played without involving the impaler.”

“I see that.” Jane breaks out into a simper.

“But I’m sure he has every intention of impaling you soon enough.”

Jane covers her reddening cheeks with her hands.

“What?” Black teases her. “I thought we were past the point of modesty. No?”

She takes her hands off of her face. “Not entirely, no.”

“But to answer your question, having control over that part of you is what’s in it for him. You are the prize. It’s a unique approach, but that’s just our lifestyle.”

“How do you mean? What kind of lifestyle permits you to have the time and resources to do this?”

“Basically, we think for ourselves. We say and do what’s right for us. It’s called independent thought, and it’s pretty addictive once you catch on.”

Jane scoffs at him. “You’re not big on giving straight answers, are you?”

“Take what you get.”

“I have been.”

“And quit trying to draw a parallel between this and some past experience.” He urges her. “There is nothing.”

A smile creeps onto Jane’s lips as Black lectures her in his strangely captivating way.

“Just trust that Cade has good intentions. You’ve seen nothing to the contrary.”

She notices that they’re nearing her apartment complex. “There’s something I haven’t figured out yet, and it’s been bugging me.” Jane jumps on her last opportunity to pry.

“What’s that?”

“Did you see the card that he sent with my instructions for tonight?”

“Yes.” Black smirks knowingly.

“What was the significance of the scales of justice?”

“He was dropping you a clue about himself.”

“A clue about himself.” Her eyes narrow down to a stare of concentration and then blaze wide open in an unsettled glare. “He’s not a lawyer, is he?”

Black doesn’t respond.

“He is a lawyer.” She concludes with disdain.

“Don’t get upset. He’s not exactly your typical lawyer.”

***

The next day, Black’s suite door is wide open. He, Hannah and Cade are spread out across his grey sectional. The living room is bright with early afternoon sun. Hannah’s bare feet are propped up on the coffee table, and her arm is stretched out along the back cushion. Black is eating a burrito.

“Yeah, I knew she’d be put off when she found out I was a lawyer. I thought it was better to get that detail out of the way.” Cade’s half-eaten burrito rests on a plate in his lap.

“It wasn’t a deal-breaker or anything.” Black sets his burrito down on a plate on the coffee table.

Hannah grimaces at the opaque black liquid oozing out of Cade’s burrito. “What is that, anyway?”

“Chicken and black bean.”

Brian is in the open doorway of Black’s suite, waiting for a break in the conversation.

Out the corner of her eye, Hannah detects his presence. “What is it, Brian?”

“Some friends of mine are getting together at the same bar I went to last week–”

“Yeah, that’s fine.” She cuts him off with a curt wave.

“Should I plan on borrowing one of the cars in the garage, or?”

“And get pulled over for drunk driving?” Hannah huffs. “I don’t think so. Get a ride from Will.”

“All right, I’ll ask him later.” Brian backs out of the doorway and heads down the penthouse corridor.

Cade points at Brian. “How’s he doing, by the way?”

“Fine. He’s still balancing everything out.”

“That’s normal. He’s still new.”

“New or not, I had him tag along with Nick on a scenario last night. It’s time for Brian to start getting his feet wet, earning his keep.” While Hannah babbles on, Random, Rayne and Ryan walk together up the penthouse corridor, passing by the open doorway...

Random looks into Black’s suite on his way by. He tunes in to eavesdrop on their conversation, but it’s just Hannah squawking nonsense, so he tunes out.

The three of them continue towards the elevator for their weekly engagement at Majestic Hills wine bar.

***

Gnarled wood covers the floor of the quaint, airy wine bar. Pub tables are scattered along the taupe walls beneath large paned windows.

A huge painting of a vineyard hangs on the wall behind the counter. The corners of the room on either side of the counter are lined with shelves full of wine bottles. Andy, the owner, steps out from behind the counter to greet Random, Rayne and Ryan when they enter the winery.

“Hello, it must be Wednesday.” Andy welcomes the trio, gesturing to their regular table. They have the place all to themselves.

“Got anything good for us today?” Random asks and takes his seat at the table alongside Rayne and Ryan. There is a sampler plate waiting for them in the middle of their table. It’s filled with a sumptuous variety of sliced cheeses, thin crackers, grapes, stuffed olives and little condiment trays.

“I always do, don’t I?” Andy brings over two empty wineglasses etched with the Majestic Hills logo. He slides one down in front of Random and one in front of Rayne.

“That you do.” She attests. He turns back to the counter and grabs the necks of two wine bottles, one red and one white.

“I just got these opened up for you.” Andy sets the bottle of white wine on the table. He picks up Random’s glass and begins pouring the red. “This is a Gothenburg cabernet. I’m very interested to hear what you think of it.” He puts the glass of wine down for Random and fills Rayne’s glass with the white. “And this here is a Gewürztraminer. I think you’ll be pleased.” With an accommodating mien, Andy puts the glass down for Rayne. He leaves both wine bottles on their table. “Relax, enjoy and I’ll check back in a bit to get your opinion.”

“Thank you, Andy,” Random says to him.

Rayne picks up her glass of Gewürztraminer while Andy disappears into his office in the back room.

Random tastes his cabernet, arching his brows in approval. He sets down the glass.

“Pretty good?” Rayne asks before tasting her own.

“Yeah, this is a good one.”

Ryan selects a stuffed olive off of the plate and glances over at Random. “When is the new bartender coming on board?”

“Uh.” Random’s attitude sours. “Never, if Black doesn’t get his head out of his ass.”

“Oh, it’s Becky?” Ryan deduces. He pops the olive into his mouth. Ryan’s the one who Black sent over to drive Becky to dinner the first night they met in person.

“That’s who it was supposed to be. And I think it’s stupid of him to let his impatience throw off a whole game plan. After investing months into a willing recruit like her.” Random picks up his wineglass. “But, he won’t hear it from me.”

“He hasn’t decided anything yet.” Ryan discloses with a guarded edge to his voice.

“Really?”

Ryan nods at him.

“So.” Rayne turns to Random. “Does Black know that Sam’s coming back?” She takes another sip of her wine.

“I don’t get that impression, but I don’t know.” He asks Ryan, “Do you know?”

“No, I have no idea. He hasn’t said a word to me about Sam coming back.”

“Well, I’m sure you know not to say anything to him.”

Ryan tilts his head at Random in offense.

“No need to patronize,” Rayne jumps in, “Ryan knows to keep his mouth shut.”

“I’m not patronizing. I’m reiterating.” Random takes a drink of his wine.

“I’ll be right back.” Ryan slides off his stool and crosses the gnarled wood floor to the restroom.

Once he’s out of earshot, Rayne resumes their conversation where it left off. She signals to the restroom. “And he doesn’t need to report anything back to you, either.” She remains composed while speaking up for her prized subordinate.

“Did I ask him to?”

“Your tone was implicit.”

“I know they’re friends, and I wouldn’t ask Ryan to spy. However I do expect him to be honest when I ask him a direct question.” Random leans back in his stool.

“And he was. But despite you keeping him on the house staff, Ryan does not reside under you.”

Random picks up his wineglass, flashing her a snarky grin. “No need to patronize, Rayne.”

“I was just reiterating, Random.”

“What do you think of that cabernet?” Andy sails in from the back room, smiling cheerfully.

“Excellent. We’ll do three cases of that, this week.” Random states.

***

Later that afternoon, a jaded Becky sits down at her computer and opens her inbox. Like usual, she does not have any new messages from Black. Becky slides her hand off of the keyboard and raises it to her face. She presses her fingertips into her forehead, exhaling her disappointment.

Becky has the two phones out on her desk. She picks up the new one and gets up from her desk chair. On her way into her bedroom, she once again calls Black to leave him a message. “Please don’t make me go back to my normal life and pretend like this never happened.” Becky wanders over to her bed. Her agony wanes, and she continues talking forthright. “But if that is the case, and if this is really over, then be decent enough to give me some closure at the very least.” Becky tosses the phone on her bed and heads back into the living room.

On her desk, her old phone begins to ring. Becky picks it up. “Hi Jackie.” She goes over to her couch.

“Hi, how are you doing?” On the other line, Jackie sounds upbeat.

“I’m fine, thanks.”

“Do you feel like you’re accomplishing what you wanted to?”

“Yeah.” Becky combs her fingers through her hair and plops down on the couch. “I mean, nothing life-changing has happened, but I guess I feel more clearheaded about what I need to do.”

“Well, that’s pretty much what you were after, right?”

“Pretty much.”

“So uh,” Jackie’s tune turns grim, “Gary wants to know if you’re coming back into work on Monday.”

“I’m sure he does.”

“I think this is the last time he’s gonna ask, Becky. If you know what I mean.”

Becky takes a moment to acknowledge Jackie’s warning. Off in the distance, her new phone starts ringing. Becky gasps. “I’ll call you right back.” She hangs up on Jackie and flings the phone down onto her couch. She runs into the bedroom.

Her new phone is sitting on her bed, lit up with an incoming call from Black. Becky immediately grabs it.

“Hi.” She stands there motionless, waiting to hear what he says.

“Can I come by to talk tonight?”

***

The crack of pool balls is heard over the energetic music playing in the background of Tiger’s lounge that night. Brian and Rob are seated next to each other at the bar. Brian reaches forward to take a fresh beer from the female bartender.

“Thanks.” He sets down his beer. The bar is about half full.

“Jackie’s gonna freak out, so be prepared.” Rob sips his whiskey and glimpses over at the door. He sees Jackie walk inside and scope out the bar. “She just came in.”

Jackie spots Rob sitting at the bar. On her way over to him, she cocks her head in uncertainty.

Brian twists around in his barstool, smiling at Jackie.

“NO way!” She marches straight up to Brian and friskily punches him in the arm. “Look who’s here.”

Brian looks past Jackie at the door. “Is it just you?”

“What the hell’s that supposed to mean?”

“Where’s Casey and Steve, and everybody?”

“Where do you think? Working late, picking up the slack for your stupid ass. Becky’s been gone, too. We’re down two of you in sales.”

“Becky’s gone too?”

“Yeah. She’s having some personal crisis, I don’t know.” Jackie slants her eyes at him. “She’s not with you, is she?”

“Wh-what?” Brian laughs out loud. “No, why would she be with me?”

“You haven’t talked to her, or anything?”

Still laughing, Brian glances over at Rob in sheer confusion. “Why would I talk to her?” he asks Jackie.

“You both just up and disappeared at the same damn time. Thanks a lot, by the way. Everybody’s been in a real bad mood around there.”

“Uh-oh, maybe I shouldn’t have come down here.”

“Just buy a few rounds, they’ll be fine.” Rob pats Brian on the back.

“I can do that.” Brian has been given a credit card for his personal expenses.

Jackie sits down in the barstool next to him. “Oh my God, I can’t believe this.” She unzips her purse. “I have GOT to call Becky.” Jackie starts digging around in her purse for her phone...

Meanwhile, Becky’s two phones are out on her desk in the living room. Her old phone vibrates with Jackie’s incoming call.

Becky doesn’t hear it. She’s in the bathroom, wrapped up in her pale pink robe. She stands across from her fogged-over mirror, toweling off her hair. The white leather thong is draped over a pair of blue fleece pants that are lying on the bathroom counter...

“She’s not picking up.” Back at Tiger’s, Jackie is on her phone, getting Becky’s voicemail. She leaves her a message. “Becky, you are not going to believe this.” Jackie ogles Brian, who’s in the midst of light conversation with Rob. “Call me back as soon as you get this, girl.” Jackie hangs up and holds the phone in her hand. “Where the hell have you been?” She interrogates Brian.

“He fell in love with a blonde goddess and took a job at her club.” Rob blurts out.

“Doing what?”

“Whatever I want, for the most part.” Brian boasts to her.

Jackie flares her nostrils. “I see. You don’t really have to work, because you’re her little boy-toy. Is that it?”

After contemplating for a second, he says, “You’re actually not that far off.”

“Oh Brian, you lead such a charmed life while the rest of us carry your load.”

The female bartender leans over the bar towards Jackie. “What can I get you, sweetie?”

“A red beer, please.”

“That reminds me, there’s this redheaded girl I work with and she’s like, throwing herself at me.” Brian brings up the subject of the Spinner.

“Ah, here we go.” Rob slumps back and sips his whiskey.

“I’m serious, though. She’s just crazy, and everybody there seems to hate her.”

“Gee, I wonder why.” Jackie mumbles sarcastically.

“Why?”

“Because she’s a slut!” She hurls out her hands, one of which is still clutching her phone.

“Then why don’t they fire her?”

“I don’t think you can fire somebody just for being a slut.” Jackie looks down at her phone. “Why isn’t Becky getting back to me?”

***

In Becky’s townhouse, the bathroom light is on, but the living room is dim. A jar candle burns on her coffee table, spreading its lavender scent through the room.

Becky walks up to her desk, dressed down in a thin white t-shirt and the pair of pale blue fleece pants that were in the bathroom. Her hair is mostly dry, and her makeup is very subtle. Becky sees the new voicemail notification on her old phone.

She picks up the phone and starts listening to the message from Jackie. “Becky, you are not going to believe this.” She can hear loud bar noise in the background of the message.

“Not this time, Jackie.” Becky promptly deletes the voicemail.

There’s a knock at the front door. She sets her phone on the desk and rushes up to answer it. Becky opens the door for Black. They lock eyes but don’t exchange a word. She steps aside and lets Black into her living room. She closes the door behind him.

Black heads over to Becky’s desk and takes a seat in her desk chair. Becky sits down cross-legged on the floor, facing him. There is a distinct air of calmness in the room. They both have sober expressions, poised for a reasonable and respectful conversation. Black starts it off.

“I don’t think this is gonna work out.”

Seemingly prepared for this statement, Becky folds her arms in her lap. “I know I said several things I shouldn’t have. And I also know that I’m clearly not meeting your expectations thus far. But I’ve had a week to think about this. And one of the first things you told me, which I have in writing, is that disobedience is the only thing that would end the game for me.”

“Correct,” he says firmly.

“And I passed the test that night. Everything I did and said from that point on was totally belligerent, and totally inappropriate. But I wasn’t disobedient during the time we were playing the game, while you were testing me. I did what you asked me to do.” Becky studies his face, but it’s inscrutable.

“And then you had a meltdown in my car.”

“Yes.” She readily admits.

“And I tried to justify it. I don’t even know why, but I did.” Black shrugs, canvassing her candlelit living room. “But the fact is, even though you are dominant by nature, I can’t bring someone in who can’t go through the process of submission.” He levels with her. “And I don’t believe you can.”

Becky maintains eye contact with Black while she meticulously and steadily makes her argument. “Had you told me earlier on, the things that you told me that night in the car, I would’ve been much less confused and more trusting. I know you couldn’t. I know that’s not how it works. But knowing what I know now, I feel like I can go through the process.”

“See, that night is a perfect example of how you can’t let go of control. You had to push me to the point of telling you more than I wanted to, when that was not your role and not your prerogative. But in order for you to get what you wanted, you had to push my buttons. And you knew that, and you did it. Though that is dominance, it’s also disobedience, whether we were actively playing the game or not.”

Taking a moment to think, Becky uncrosses her legs and bends her knees up. She plants the soles of her feet on the carpet in front of her. She looks up at him receptively. “Okay. I just really needed you to help me understand and give me that little extra push, to trust you fully.” Becky wraps her arms around her shins and rests her chin on her knees. “Submission, it’s nothing like how I’m wired. I’m not gonna lie. It’s a very unnatural way for me to be after living on my own and being in control of things for so long.”

“I know.”

“If you can take that into consideration, is there any way for you to make an exception and give me a second chance?” Becky asks him through an apologetic and endearing stare.

Black remains aloof. “Have you gone back to work?”

“No, but you should already know that. Unless you stopped tracking me.” Becky retreats after verbalizing that possibility.

“Have you taken the ring out?”

She bares a diffident smile. “No.”

“Becky, I know that this is a very emotionally charged situation. I’ve been through it myself.”

She nods at him.

“So, I don’t blame you for getting emotional and asking questions. But I do read between the lines, and I can spot things in people.”

Becky appears unsure of where he’s going with this. “Okay...” She listens with marked interest.

“You’re not an objective person. That’s a huge detriment in this game and this lifestyle in general.”

“Please don’t take that one bad conversation and make generalizations.”

“It’s not a generalization based on one conversation, though.” He counters her. “And objectivity is not the easiest thing to just adopt because somebody tells you to.”

“I think it’s something that I could develop through my submission, if I’m given the chance. I also think that if I could be objective in my work role,” Becky sticks one finger out to pontificate, “which I was,” she curls her finger back in. “Then I can also be in this role as well.”

Black crosses his arms together over his stomach. The vibe between them grows dense with dejection.

“I...” He shakes his head. “I just don’t think you’re right for me, Becky.”

The amber centers of her eyes flare in panic. Her arms slide off her shins and fall to her sides. “No–”

Chapter 4

Seated in her desk chair, Black looks down at Becky on the floor. Her arms hang flaccid at her sides, shoulders slouched, starkly crestfallen.

“That’s the adrenaline.” Marsa takes the bags of shoeboxes over to the open closet. She plants her butt down on the floor and begins pulling shoeboxes out of the bags.

“I can’t thank you two enough. You’ve been more than hospitable to me, today.”

“Trust me, it was just as big of a rush for us. Now let’s get you settled in.” Minya selects a champagne-colored tank dress that has an embossed rose pattern. “This is what you should wear to the party tomorrow.”

“The party?”

“Yeah, every Saturday is a big bash around here. This week’s theme is like a New Orleans masquerade ball, and this dress will be fantastic.” Minya carries the dress over to hang it up in the closet.

“Oh, okay.”

Minya leans over top of Marsa to grab a hanger for the dress.

“Hey, where’s that cute swimsuit you got?” Down on the floor, Marsa is busy lining up new pairs of shoes in the closet. She glimpses over at Babe.

“I haven’t found it yet.” Babe is hunched over a shopping bag, digging out handfuls of lacy bras and panties to replace her cotton basics.

“Find it. We should go down to the pool for a while before dinner.”

***

Later that night at Becky’s townhouse, she is seated across from Black at her dining room table. A three-candle candelabrum in the center of her table illuminates their plates of eaten chicken parmesan. Becky is dressed up in a yellow, wrap-style sundress while Black is dressed down in a black hooded sweatshirt and jeans.

“That was good, thank you.”

“You’re welcome.” Becky is noticeably pleased to have his company, but she keeps her composure in front of Black, who’s his typical unruffled self. “Are you ever gonna tell me your real name?”

Black shakes his head. “It doesn’t matter. This isn’t a regular relationship, Becky.”

“I know. I’m well aware of that.”

“Then quit trying to get to know me.” Black reaches down to subtly inspect the arms of Becky’s wood dining room chair. “I’ll tell you things when they’re relevant.”

“Okay.” Becky picks up the open bottle of red wine on the table and begins filling their glasses. “Is there anything relevant you can tell me about the game, then?”

“Yes. You cannot just focus on the end goal of being a Dominant. Submission’s not a ‘thing’, it’s a state of being. If you’re not present in the moment, none of it matters.”

Becky finishes pouring the wine and sets the bottle down.

“And then you don’t really, change, in any positive ways.”

“I understand that.”

“I don’t know that you do.” He laughs softly. “I honest to God don’t.”

Starry-eyed, Becky speaks in a cajoling lilt. “But you’ll give me a test?”

“That’s why I’m here.”

***

Meanwhile at the Mercer Estate, Random is sitting alone by the fire pit, on the phone. He has a drink in his other hand. The surrounding patio area is empty and quiet.

Random leans forward in his Adirondack chair and glances down into the fire pit where the last smoldering embers glow in the bottom. “I remember when you got here, Quinn, thinking ‘man, this girl really knows what she wants’. And it was such a striking contrast to how I came in here, myself.” He eases back into his chair. “I had to be convinced of a reality that you knew before you even heard of this place.”

“I’m sure Sam was quite convincing.” Quinn implies on the other line, bold but tempered.

“Yeah, she was, but that’s the thing. She had to be, because I fought the idea that I was better suited for this life. But not you.”

“Nope.”

“You were drawn to this before you even understood it. And Black’s recruit is just like that. Except she needs a governess, someone to open up to.”

“Okay, what’s the main objective?”

“Finding her weak spot. We need to know how to break her, Quinn.”

chapters.content:
Chapter 5

Becky is facing the wall, near her dining room table. Her palms are flattened out on the wall in front of her. The candelabrum flickers in the background. Their empty dinner plates and wineglasses are still sitting out on her dining room table.

“Submission...” Black is standing behind Becky. He’s cradling her right ankle in his right hand. Black gradually pulls up on Becky’s ankle, stretching her thigh muscles. “It’s a state of being for eighty percent of the people I coexist with.” He lowers Becky’s bare foot back down to the floor.

She looks over her shoulder at him and asks, “You mean where you live?”

Black runs his fingers up the backs of Becky’s arms to her palms slapped against the wall. He takes her wrists in his hands. “Yes.” Holding her wrists, Black guides Becky’s arms down to her sides and presses her about the subject of submission. “Tell me what you learned about it.” He backs up, pulling Becky’s wrists out behind her. He crosses her arms behind her back to stretch out her shoulders.

“It’s relinquishing control and being lost in the moment. Focusing only on what’s happening next.”

“And?”

“And, wanting nothing else but to just do what you ask, in the moment.”

Black bends forward to peer down the front of Becky’s yellow sundress. “What are you wearing under this?” He lets go of Becky’s wrists and steps backwards.

“A bra and underwear.” She turns around to face him. “Regular underwear.” As opposed to the white leather thong.

“Take off the dress,” Black says bluntly on his way over to her patio door.

Vulnerable but compliant, Becky reaches back and begins unzipping her dress. She pauses when she sees Black sliding open the patio door.

“Go pull your hair up and I’ll meet you in the bedroom.” He takes a lighter out of his jeans pocket, steps outside and slides the door shut.

***

Downtown at Matt’s loft apartment, Jane stands across from him at the door. She has her canvas shopping bag filled with leftover chowder, along with her purse.

“I’m glad we could do this.” Matt gives Jane a friendly hug goodbye.

“Me too.” She returns his hug. “Thanks again for listening to my sordid story. You’re really the only person I can talk to about any of that.”

“Hey anytime,” he tells her, heartfelt, “I mean it.”

“Thanks Matt.” Jane opens the door to leave. She rides the elevator down to the ground level and heads outside to the parking lot. Her car is parked under a bright streetlamp.

Jane gets in behind the wheel of her white BMW and pulls the door shut. She sets her purse and canvas bag on the passenger seat and lingers before driving home. Skimming the quiet parking lot, Jane takes her phone out of her purse.

She starts typing a message to Cade...

At the Mercer Estate, Reno’s going down the basement corridor to chamber 3. He stops outside the door and listens for a moment but doesn’t hear anything. He takes one last sweep down the corridor before slowly turning the doorknob.

Reno skulks into chamber 3. He halts suddenly when he sees Cade.

Cade’s on the opposite side of the exam table, facing the door. “Hey.” He leers quizzically at Reno in the doorway. “What are you doing?” he asks through a laugh.

Reno notes the variety of suspension cuffs lined up on the exam table in front of Cade. “I think the better question is what are you doing?” He steps into the chamber and peruses the array of black leather cuffs on display.

“I’m planning out my main event for the suspension performance tomorrow night.”

“Oh yeah.” Reno recalls. “Hence the cable wire and turnbuckle hook you wanted.” He walks over to the exam table and picks up a wrist suspension cuff with a metal ring stitched into the palm. “Making a human puppet, are you?”

Cade nods at him. Reno slips an index finger through the metal ring, hanging the cuff from his finger.

“Like a marionette.” Cade motions to the doorway. “Why’d you sneak in here like that?”

“Oh, I didn’t think anybody’d be in here tonight.”

“Nobody was, which is why I’m using it.” Cade shoots him a curious look. “Do you need me to vacate?”

Though it’s evident that Reno had intentions for chamber 3 tonight, he shrugs off Cade’s offer. “Nah you’re fine.”

Cade’s phone is lying on the end of the exam table. It vibrates and lights up with a notification. Cade grabs his phone and reads the message. “Huh.”

“What?” When Reno spots the smirk forming on Cade’s face, he sets the wrist cuff down on the exam table.

“A text from Jane asking me ‘what’s the alternative to refraining?’”

“I take it she’s embracing the game.”

“Yeah.” He replies with a hint of surprise.

“Frisky little thing.”

Cade calls Jane. While it rings, he tells Reno, “Unfortunately, I don’t really have time to play tonight.”

“I bet you’ll make some time,” Reno says under his breath and hangs around to listen in on Cade’s phone call.

“Hello?” Jane answers on the other line.

“It’s not a punishment, you know?” Cade backs away from the exam table and wanders through the chamber with his phone to his ear.

“It’s not a prize, either.”

“There’s a point to it.”

“I apologize for being greedy.”

Cade formulates an impromptu plan. “I’m gonna send you a location and I want you to drive there, right now.” He heads for the chamber door. “When you get there, park next to my truck and get into the driver side backseat. Okay?”

“Okay.”

***

Back at Becky’s townhouse, Black walks into her bedroom, relaxed from the joint he smoked outside. He flips on the light and sees Becky.

She’s standing off to the side of her bed in a pink bra and underwear. She has her hands clasped behind her back. Her hair is up in a ponytail.

“Why are you standing here in the dark?”

“I don’t know.” Becky’s mouth twitches in an attempt to keep a straight face. She fidgets with nervous excitement.

“Okay.” Black assesses her behavior. She’s skittish. He backs out of the doorway and drags one of Becky’s dining room armchairs into the middle of her bedroom.

Becky watches Black bring a second armchair into her room. He sets it down next to the first chair. Then he goes over by her treadmill and casually says,

“Go into the top drawer of your dresser and bring me the ropes.”

“I-I don’t have any ropes in my dresser.” She stammers.

“There should be two. Are you relinquishing control and being lost in the moment?”

Baring a mystified smile, Becky circles around her bed to open the top drawer of her dresser. She scoops out the two 20’ white nylon ropes inside. Becky carries the ropes over to Black, who drapes one of them on the side rail of her treadmill. He loops the other rope loosely around his hand a few times.

Black weaves the rope ends through the loops, forming the knot for a leg shackle. “Lift your right leg up.”

She grips the side rail of the treadmill and raises her right foot. Black leans down to slip the shackle over Becky’s foot and up her leg. He stops it just above her knee and holds onto the loose ends of the rope.

“You can put it down.”

Becky lowers her foot to the floor.

Black runs his free hand up the back of her leg and slides two fingers under the shackle. Stroking Becky’s thigh with his thumb, he tugs back on the silky rope and tightens the knot.

She fully tunes into the tension, placid and intrigued. His fingers under the rope prevent the shackle from pinching too tightly around her leg.

He pulls his fingers out from under it. Black rises up, drops the rope and proceeds towards the dining room chairs. “Get over here.” Black stops behind the armchair that’s facing Becky’s bed. While she rushes over, he directs her. “Come kneel on the front edge of this chair.”

Becky kneels on the dining room chair cushion. She clutches the wood armrests and looks up at Black standing behind it. Her calves hang off the front end of the chair; her back is to the bed.

Black drags the second armchair up closer and has a seat. He collects the loose ends of rope hanging from Becky’s leg shackle. Separating the two ropes, he draws them around the front leg of the chair. He ties a square knot under the armrest’s base to serve as an anchor for her next binding.

He glances up at Becky. “Lay your forearms down on the armrests.” Black gives her clear instructions in a mild tone.

With her right knee now tied off to the front leg of the chair, Becky lays her right forearm down flat on the armrest. She watches Black bring the rope up through the inside of the armrest, closest to her elbow. He wraps it around her forearm, hooks his finger under it and lifts it up, pushing the end of the rope through the loop.

He pulls it through and asks, “Do you want to know something about me?”

“Of course I do.”

Black rhythmically keeps wrapping the rope around Becky’s arm, forming a loop with his finger and pulling the rope through. He gradually weaves a knotted wrap around Becky’s forearm, binding it to the arm of the chair. “This is something I really like to do.”

“Playing with ropes?”

“Tying...bondage.” He calmly corrects her.

“Okay.”

The knotted wrap reaches Becky’s wrist, at the backside of the chair. Black draws the loose ends of rope down and around the back leg to tie a square knot, leaving the right side of her body neatly tethered to the chair.

Black stands up and takes Becky’s chin in his hand. “How does that feel?”

“It feels fine.” She stares up at him, fawning affectionately. “You obviously know what you’re doing, don’t you?”

Black lets go of Becky’s chin. He fights back a slight smile. “Don’t try and flatter me.” He picks up the second armchair and moves it over to Becky’s left side. Black goes over to the treadmill to get the other white rope. “You’re not getting any, tonight.” He heads back over to Becky.

“Well, that’s nothing new.” She banters with Black, who walks behind her chair and stops in front of her dangling calves. She looks over her shoulder at him.

“I mean nothing.” Black reaches down to tap Becky between the legs with the back of his hand. He glances at her face. “Nothing.”

Becky demurely slides her left leg over to her bound one. She squeezes her thighs together.

Black continues around to the empty chair beside her. He pulls the white nylon rope through his closed fist, gliding his hand to its center to start the second leg shackle.

***

At that same time, Jane’s BMW rolls down an unlit curvy road through a city park to its public boat launch area. A row of parking stalls faces the waterline. All of the stalls are empty except for the one Cade’s SUV is parked in.

Jane parks next to the SUV. Her lights go off. She gets out of her car and goes around to the driver side of the SUV.

When she approaches the truck, she finds the backdoor cracked open. Rightfully precarious, she curls her fingers around the door handle and opens it up. Jane peeks into the backseat. She’s alleviated to see Cade sitting there.

“Oh good, it’s you.”

“Yeah, this one’s unplanned. Get in.” Cade holds out his hand to help her up.

Jane takes his hand and steps up onto the side rail. She swings her left leg over Cade’s thighs. She plants her knees on the seat and straddles his lap before grasping onto his shoulders.

He pulls the door shut. The interior lights fade out.

Jane centers on Cade as he runs his palms up her sides. The energy between them is charged. Her faint pants cut through the intense silence.

“Put your hands on your thighs.”

She lets go of his shoulders and clenches her upper thighs.

Cade takes her cheeks in his hands. “We’re gonna play a real simple little game that we can do right here in the truck.”

“Okay,” she whispers, incited by the idea.

“Whatever I ask you, your answer is ‘yes’, no matter what. Will you do that?”

“Yes.”

He brings her face in closer to his. “Can I kiss you?”

“Yes.” Jane collapses into a deep but evanescent kiss until Cade pulls away.

He lets go of her cheeks and asks, “Do you trust me?”

“Yes I do.” She solemnly proclaims.

Cade grazes his fingers across Jane’s back, over her bra strap. “Is it all right if I take this off, then?” He glimpses up at her.

“Yes.”

He slips his hands up the back of Jane’s shirt to undo her bra. “You’re awfully compliant today, aren’t you?” he asks, smiling.

“Yes.” She’s also smiling.

Cade slides his hands out of Jane’s shirt. He rests one hand on her shoulder while his other one dives between her legs. Cade pinches the crotch fabric of Jane’s pants and pulls it down, away from her body. “Are you gonna let me ruin these pants?”

Gritting her teeth, she answers, “Yes.”

He uses both hands to rip the center seam out of Jane’s pants. She squeezes her eyes shut until he’s done tearing them. Cade reaches up for the sides of her neck. He pulls her in close. “Do you want to keep going?”

“Yes.”

He leans in to kiss her, and Jane responds avidly. He drags his palms down her neck to her shoulders and gently pushes her away, breaking out of their kiss.

Cade looks up at her. “Can you put your arms behind your back for me?”

“Yes.”

“Bend your elbows up.”

Jane bends her arms behind her back, crossing her hands together between her shoulder blades.

Cade reaches around to grab Jane’s wrists. He brings her body down into his chest. Her head hangs over his shoulder.

He slides his other hand down her ass and up into the hole in her pants, seizing her crotch from behind.

She sucks in a sharp breath of anticipation.

“Do you want me to stop?”

Jane expels a shuddering gasp of disappointment. She doesn’t answer him.

Cade removes his hand from Jane’s pants then lets go of her wrists. He steers her off of his lap and sits her down on the seat beside him. “I’ll take that as a ‘yes’.”

“Are you leaving?”

“I want you to hold off for a while. Otherwise you’re gonna mess up my plans. I’m not kidding.”

“That doesn’t mean you have to leave.” Jane clings onto Cade’s thigh.

He puts his hand on top of hers. “I’ve got to go. I have other things to do tonight.”

“Oh.” Instantly forlorn, she yanks her hand away.

“Hey.” Cade reaches up for Jane’s face and strokes her cheek. “Don’t worry, it’s nothing like this.” He strays off in consideration. “Well, it kind of is, but it’s not for me.” Cade comes clean. “I need to go return a favor.”

“Aha.” Jane is utterly relieved. Thanks to Black, she understands what Cade means by a favor. “Is it for anyone I know?”

Cade nods. “Mm-hmm.”

“Okay.”

***

Back at Becky’s townhouse, her left knee and forearm are bound to the dining room chair in the same fashion as her right side. Black is wrapping the loose ends of rope around the back leg of the chair and tying a square knot. When he tightens that knot, the tie is complete. Her knees are tethered to the front corners of the chair, and her forearms are wrapped to its arms.

Black stands up from his own chair. He walks in front of Becky’s face and studies his work. His clean rows of white rope hug at just the right tension to allow shifting under the restriction of her arm gauntlets. The tight knots securing her leg shackles to the chair keep her posed in a relatively comfortable kneel. She gazes up at Black’s dark eyes reviewing her bound body.

“Tell me.” He grips the base of Becky’s head, just below her ponytail. “How do you feel?”

“Incapacitated,” she says through a sultry sigh.

“What do you think is gonna happen?”

“I really don’t know.”

“You have no control over it, either.”

“That’s true.” She acquiesces.

The sound of the front door closing startles Becky. She gasps at Black, who asks,

“What’s the matter, Becky?”

“That was my front door.”

“Do I seem surprised?” Black lets go of Becky’s head and turns away.

“What are you doing?” She frets, watching him.

He answers her on his way out of the room. “You trust me, right? You made it pretty clear the other night that you do.” Black’s voice trails off as he leaves the bedroom.

“Oh God.” Becky drops her head down. Her hair swishes over her reddening cheeks.

Cade enters the bedroom with a thick book tucked under his arm. He picks up the empty dining room chair Black was using and drags it over to face Becky.

She can hear someone moving through the bedroom but is reluctant to check and see who’s there, attesting to her level of self-consciousness.

When the front door slams shut in the living room, her need to know wins over. Becky lifts her head and fixes on Cade, who’s sitting down in the chair directly across from her. He flashes her a curt smile, completely indifferent to her state of immobility.

“And who are you?” she asks.

“My name’s Cade. I go by my name.” He points out while setting the book on her nightstand.

“Okay, is that rare?”

“I’d say it’s about fifty-fifty. I didn’t get the whole ‘name’ thing at first, I’ll be honest. But now, I see how it can trigger a mindset.” He grants and crosses his legs. “Anyway, the reason I’m here is to do you a favor.”

“Is that so?” Becky bats her lashes at Cade, displaying emphatic skepticism.

“It is. I’m gonna help you prove to our mutual friend that you’re in this for the right reasons and not just to get off.”

Roundly appalled, she asks, “Did he tell you everything?”

“What are you talking about? The clit ring?”

Becky’s face crumples with indignity.

“You have to admit, everything so far has been centered around your gash there, hasn’t it?”

“Oh my God.” She blares out a moan. “Could you be more crude?”

“Yes, much.” Cade chuckles.

Becky stares at him through the heavy-lidded eyes of disgrace. “Please don’t. I have never been so embarrassed in my life.”

“But you don’t have to be.” He reassures her in an upbeat attitude. “This is trivial compared to the things I see and do on a normal day. That’s the upside to trusting people.” He illustrates for her. “You get to find out about some weird shit that people like to do. But, I digress.” Cade reaches for the book on the nightstand and sets it in his lap. “Like I said, we’re going to prove him wrong.” He bows in towards Becky, seething confidence. “And we are.” He leans back. “Once we do, you’ll pass the test and win the prize.”

“Let me guess, you can’t tell me what the prize is, though.”

“I do whatever I please.”

“Well, then do you care to tell me?”

“It’s something you want pretty badly.” Cade taunts her. “Something you’ve already asked him about.”

“I’ve asked him about a lot of things. Can you be a little more specific?”

“Sure. It’s an invitation to the house.”

Becky gawks at him, flat out thunderstruck. “THE house?”

“Mm-hmm.” Cade affirms.

Becky arches her brows and huffs. Taken aback by this bombshell, she assents. “Okay, you’re right, that’s a big prize. What do I have to do?” She wiggles her bound arms. “I mean, on top of this?”

“This?” Cade flippantly refers to Becky’s bondage. “This is nothing. He’ll do this to you all the time.”

“Good to know.”

“Sometimes submission is about putting up with things that you’d rather not. Things that have very little, if anything, to do with your own happiness.”

Becky nods in understanding.

Cade picks up the book in his lap. “Now this here, Becky, is a book about consent in the law. Fortunately for me, that can be a real grey area. You see, this is a subject I had to study up on recently. I didn’t quite get done reading though, so we’re gonna finish this up tonight.”

“Okay,” she says, notably unenthused.

He cracks open the book and begins flipping through the pages, searching for the spot he left off on. “Before we start, how are you doing? Need a drink or anything?”

“No, I’m fine right now.”

“Hope you don’t need to use the bathroom.” Cade glances up at her.

“I don’t, but that’s also why I don’t want anything to drink.”

“Okay. Then before we get started, you get to ask me one question.” He finds his page and opens the book up on his knee.

“Is Black coming back here tonight?”

“No.” Cade looks down at the book.

Becky frowns. “All right, let’s go.”

***

Meanwhile, it’s daytime in Amsterdam, and Sam is seated at her desk in front of her large monitor. A fresh cappuccino steams lightly on the desk. Morning sun spills into the bedroom. Her empty black bookshelf is in the background, as well as her unmade bed with the Velvet Underground picture hanging on the wall above it. Sam puts her phone on speaker and sets it on the desk next to her keyboard.

“I hope you know the only reason I get on here is for your amusement.” Black’s remark comes through her phone.

Scoffing at him, Sam reaches over to click open her infamous message board, which fills the monitor with lines of text. “Yeah I know. You hate the internet, but you’re on it all the time.” She scans the current conversation rolling down her screen.

“No, I’m really not. I use it to visit you, and when it’s the logical means to an end. Otherwise, I avoid it like the cesspool of people’s opinions that it is.”

“Cesspool, huh?”

“Yes, the drain that sucks the imagination and mystery out of life as we once knew it.”

“You were born in the wrong decade.” Sam blows the steam off of her cappuccino.

“I definitely was.” He verifies. They’ve discussed that notion at length. “But using an antiquated platform doesn’t mean you don’t embrace it at all.”

“This message board, it’s just been something fun to do since I’ve been out here.”

“Oh, give me a break,” Black says through a laugh. “You did this before you ever arrived at this company to begin with.”

“True.” With a conceding tip of her head, Sam starts typing.

“So, what is it about this board? The whole concept, what’s the draw for you?”

“It’s not like I’m the only one,” she tells Black...

He is slumped lazily in his desk chair with his phone up to his ear, waiting for Cade to get back from Becky’s townhouse. His laptop is opened up on the desk. Sam’s message board is open on his screen. The wall sconces are dimmed down low, and a trippy tune quivers through his office. “I’m only talking about you though, Sam.”

“Okay. First of all, it’s only when I don’t have better things to do. Always has been. You know that. Secondly, it allows me to keep my brain nimble to the anonymous wiles of idiots.”

Smiling, he reads Sam’s last post while listening to her reasons on the other line.

“Thirdly, it lets me exercise my acting muscles in the absence of scenarios.”

“Speaking of, why’d you say you wouldn’t be allowed to do them when you get back?”

“Oh, I probably shouldn’t have said anything. I’ll just need to figure a way around that.”

“But why?” He persists.

“Because evidently it’s a tricky balance to be a head of the house and a face in scenes. It wasn’t a big deal back in the day, but I guess now it is. I’m sure you know that since you fall into that category.”

“It’s an unwritten rule, mainly for the guys, since we do the majority of them.”

“Then I’m confident I’ll be able to find a loophole to the rule.”

***

Driving home from Becky’s, Cade turns at a vacant intersection onto Mercer Ave. He reaches over into the passenger seat of his SUV to get his phone and call Jane.

“Hello?” she answers.

“I wish I didn’t have to run off on you, earlier.” Cade drives up the dark road which is thick with trees and lacking other cars.

“Did you return your favor?”

“I did. What are you doing?”

“Wondering when I’ll get to see you again.”

“Hmm, insatiable.” He comments.

“And intrigued.”

“Well, there is something I wanted to run by you earlier, but I didn’t have time.”

“What’s that?”

Cade slows down to pull into the driveway of the Mercer Estate. He heads up the long driveway to the row of garage doors. “There’s a party here tomorrow night, but it wouldn’t be your typical meet and greet, or anything. I have a certain way I’d like to introduce you,” he tells Jane...

The lights are on in her quiet bathroom. Jane is lying in a frothy bubble bath with her phone up to her ear. A glass of red wine sits on the edge of the tub.

“That comes as no surprise. Run it by me.” Jane’s face reflects a dreamy expression while she listens to Cade describe how and when she would be picked up for the party. As he goes on about the evening, the whimsy fades from her eyes and acute insecurity sets in. She takes a deep breath. “I’m not so sure about that, Cade. I just can’t imagine seeing all of those new people for the first time and having them see me, like that, for the first time.” She explains her resistance to Cade...

He steps into the penthouse corridor. The elevator doors close behind him. “You realize you’ll be blindfolded, right? You won’t see a thing.”

“Ohh.” She moons on the other line like a weight has been lifted. “That wouldn’t be as bad, then.”

“Exactly.” Cade walks down the corridor to Black’s suite. “If you can’t see it, it’s not there.”

“Will I ever get to see your house?”

“Of course you will.” He opens Black’s suite door and steps inside. “But not tomorrow.” He lowers his voice. “Listen, be ready at eight. I’ve gotta go.” Cade ends the call and browses the living room. Kaime is sitting by herself on the grey sectional, watching a movie.

She looks over her shoulder at Cade. “Hi.”

“Where’s he at?”

“In his office.” Kaime advises Cade and gets back to her movie.

Inside the office, Black rotates his chair away from the laptop screen to his opening door.

“Why didn’t you answer your phone?” Cade closes the door behind him.

Black’s holding his phone in his hand. “Because I’m on the phone.”

Cade peers around Black’s desk chair and sees Sam’s message board open on his monitor. “I see what you’re doing,” he tells him in a surmising tone. “Anyway, Becky accepted the challenge, just as you suspected.” He leans against the wall across from Black, next to the pub table barstool.

“Was she happy about the prize?”

“She was beside herself.”

“How’d she do?”

“She stayed awake through over a hundred pages of legal jargon, so...”

“Good.” Black acknowledges and then excuses him. “I’ll see you tomorrow.”

With a shrewd grin, Cade leaves the office.

Once he’s gone, Black raises his phone to his ear. “Sorry about that, Sam.” He spins back around to his monitor.

“What was all that?”
