Becky stands in the doorway and scouts out the lounge. She homes in on Black, who’s seated at the end of the bar against the wall. He waves Becky over to the empty barstool next to his.

Her face lights up. She strides up to him. “Hey.”

“How are you?” Black reaches for Becky’s beaded leash. He wraps it around his hand, and Becky slides onto the barstool.

“I am speechless,” she tells him. “The day has come.”

“What day is that?”

“The day I thank you for coming into my life.” Becky laces her arm through Black’s.

“Oh, that day.”

From behind the bar, Ryan approaches them with a smile.

Becky does a double take; it’s Ryan the driver. “Well, hi.”

“Do you need anything to drink?” he asks her.

“No, I’m good, thank you.”

Ryan courteously backs away and moves on down the bar. Black glances down at Becky.

“What do you want to do?”

She sways into Black, projecting her lust. “I saw a vacant room just across the hall.” Becky runs her hand up the sleeve of his charcoal skiff jacket.

“What are you getting at?” He scrutinizes her.

“I think it’s a good time to consummate our unconventional relationship.”

Black removes Becky’s hand from his arm.

“Please don’t reject me, just this once. It would be the perfect end to this night.”

“It’s not in the cards for us, Becky.”

“What? How is it not in the cards?”

“Look, I’ll prove it to you.” Black takes her jaw in his hands and draws her face close to his.

In sheer anticipation, Becky stops breathing. When Black leans in, Becky ardently reciprocates. Her lush mouth clashes with a turgid and unfelt kiss. No sparks seem to ignite.

Black goes through the motions until Becky pulls away in defeat. She peers up at him cynically.

“You’re right. You were trying to prove a point.”

“Are you saying I rigged it?” he asks, bemused by her accusation.

“That’s what I think.”

Black shakes his head and consoles her. “It’s nothing against you, Becky. We just have different intentions.”

“No. I can’t accept that the person who reminded me how to feel...has no feelings for me.”

“When you bring people into this life, there just isn’t a lot of room for emotions. And it’s not because you don’t want there to be–”

“Yeah, I know. It’s a game.” She interjects impotently. “I understand.”

“Do you?”

Becky nods, like yeah, she ‘gets it’.

“Want to get back into it, then?”

“Sure.” She hides her embarrassment, keeping her head turned away from him while she slides off the barstool.

But he sees it. In a droll tone he asks, “Do you need a hug?”

“I do.”

“All right.” Black stands up from his barstool. With a snarky smile, he takes Becky into his arms. She sinks into Black’s chest, soaking up his gesture of affection before they leave the lounge to join the party in the great room...

Random looks up at Jane’s suspended body. He’s standing off to the side of the fountain, holding a glass of whiskey. The murmur of conversation fills the air.

In front of Random, two 7’ tall by 6’ wide walk-through scaffold frames are set up on the great room floor, on either side of Jane. The frame legs are secured inside base plates, and suspension hooks are fastened inside the arches, rendering them suspension frames. Hanging inside each frame is a male and a female sub. Both are tied in the same flight position as Jane, facing opposite directions (east and west). However the subs are tied with ropes, and each has a chest harness in place of a waist cuff for center support. Cade is nearby keeping tabs on the three performance pieces.

Random turns away from the suspension frames to check out the east wing corridor. Through the crowd, he sees Black and Becky exiting the lounge. Random cuts through the great room and heads over to them.

Becky walks alongside Black towards the fountain. The beaded leash hangs down the middle of her back. Becky squints when she sees the delivery guy waltzing up to them, the one who carried the Mont Blanc pen and drove the fake delivery van. Her emerging grin is a cross between baffled and humored. She last saw him on her front porch saying, “Hi, I’ve got a delivery here for Rebecca Martin.” The familiar faces are like puzzle pieces slowly coming together.

“Becky, this is Random.” Black introduces her.

“Random?” Becky freezes. When she went back to Exotica tattoo parlor to talk to Alice, she’d asked her, “Do you happen to know what ‘random’ means, on the phone?” To which Alice replied, “Random is actually the nickname of the guy who heads up the collective.”

“I’d say it’s nice to meet you, but.” Random extends his hand to her.

“Yes, we’ve met.” Becky shakes his hand.

Reno races up beside Random, discernably tense.

“Oh, hey.” Oblivious to Reno’s urgency, Becky points at him with a vivacious twinkle. “Reno.”

“What?” He frowns at Becky.

“I know your name.”

“Congratulations.” He gets back to Random. “I need to talk to you.” Reno ushers Random away, directing him to the coffeeshop...

At the far end of the narrow coffeeshop, in the temple-like cabana seating area, Babe is pale as a ghost. Tears stream down her cheeks. Beside her, Trip’s lying back on the heap of indigo pillows.

Trip is unconscious.

Babe addresses Random coming up to her. “Somethin’s wrong, help him!” She scoots away from Trip when Reno and Random step in.

Random grabs onto Trip’s wrists and drags him out of the pile of pillows. Reno reaches for Trip’s feet and they carry him, upside down, to the doorway.

Babe stays right behind them. “What’s wrong with him? What’s happenin’?” She follows them through the coffeeshop to the doorway.

“He’s OD’ing, Babe. We’ll get it under control,” Random tells her.

Black is right outside the coffeeshop door waiting for them. He has his phone up to his ear, talking to Shay. “Pull a truck up front. Right now. It’s Trip.” He hangs up.

Random and Reno haul Trip out of the coffeeshop into the corridor. Babe comes out after them, jittering anxiously.

“Need any help?” Black asks Random.

“Yeah, clear a path.”

Black slides his phone into his pocket and leads the way, parting the crowd that’s gathering in the corridor. While he steers his way through the assembly, he’s surrounded by the low hum of worried comments. “Come on, move please. Get out of their way.”

Random and Reno carry Trip through the great room to the front door. Black is clearing the path in front of them, and Babe is trailing behind.

“No, how could this be?” She belts out over the music. “He just smoked a little hash!”

“It’s not the hash, Babe.” Random looks at Reno. “Call an ambulance from the truck and have them meet you.”

In the background, Shay is sprinting out the front door. She leaves it open behind her.

Black steps off to the side as Random and Reno take Trip’s limp body out the front door. He canvasses the great room and spots Becky by the fountain, frozen still. Black jogs over to her.

Becky recognizes an unanticipated familiar face off in the distance, near the patio door, while Black approaches her with a flinch of concern. He sees what she’s seeing.

Collared and standing behind Hannah, Brian is in line at the kitchen serving window.

“No.” Becky winces in disbelief. She forges ahead towards Brian for a closer look.

Black steps up behind her and wraps his arms around her shoulders. He pulls Becky back into his chest. “It’s him.”

Wholly distressed, Becky gapes at Brian across the room.

Behind them, Jane’s suspended body is gracefully lowered down to the marble floor.

***

In the meantime, Shay clenches the steering wheel of her Cayenne, focused on the road. Before they got into the truck, she alerted Reno that her best guess is some kind of opioid.

Reno’s in the front passenger seat with his phone up to his ear, calling for an ambulance.

Trip is in the backseat, slumped over with his head in Babe’s lap. She slowly combs her fingers through his thick hair.

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.content:
Chapter 6

Things are back to normal in the great room after the brief disruption with Trip. The confusion amongst the crowd has died down, and the sensually decadent vibe of the party has returned. Some guests are filing through the room on their way into the east wing corridor while others head outside.

The suspension performance is over. The frames on the floor have been removed, and the cable wire has been taken down from the metal frame of the glass ceiling. Brian has gone outside with Hannah, so he’s no longer in Becky’s line of vision.

She’s sitting on the base of the fountain, letting sporadic drops of water hit the backs of her bare shoulders. After giving her some time to lament, Black circles back around to the fountain. He stands across from Becky, blocking her view of the glass patio door, and holds out his hand.

“Come on.” Black helps her up onto her feet. “Do you want to leave?” he simply asks.

“No, I want him to leave.” Her voice strains. “Wh-why? Why is he here?” 

“He’s involved with somebody here.”

Becky casts her eyes down to the white marble floor between them. “Just, please tell me you didn’t plan this.”

“I didn’t.”

“If this is all some big mind game,” she pleads with him, “I don’t want to play.”

“It’s not. I promise you, Brian being here has nothing to do with you.”

Confounded by his claim, Becky glances up at Black. “An odd coincidence?”

“Exactly.”

She folds her arms together, still in doubt. “It’s L.A. Out of the millions of people who live here—”

“It wasn’t planned.” Black steps towards Becky. He clasps her shoulders, triggering eye contact. “That is not the type of game I play, and I’m being straight with you.” He bores into her, completely serious.

Becky bites at her lower lip, taking in his genuine demeanor. “Okay.” She starts trying to make sense of the situation by asking questions to fill in the blanks. “So, he’s just here tonight then?”

“No.” Black slides his hands off of Becky’s shoulders. “He lives here.”

“Oh my God,” she says through an embittered gasp. Becky’s hands fly up to her cheeks. “How? How does he live here?” The upbeat, jazzy music flicking through the air is almost like a parody to Becky’s surge of blindsiding angst.

Black clutches Becky’s wrists and removes her hands from her face. “Do you want to leave?”

“No, I don’t want to leave,” she answers in desperate frustration.

“Then come on, let’s get a drink and talk.”

***

Reno treads down a wide sidewalk between an open grass area and the hospital parking lot, smoking a cigarette. He has his phone up to his ear. The sidewalk is lit by in-ground path lighting. “Is anybody out on the road right now?”

“I can pull Ryan out of the bar.” Random offers on the other line.

“Yes.” Reno sounds grateful, eager to leave the hospital. “Have him swing by the hospital and get me.”

“Sure.”

***

Cade is behind the wheel of his SUV with Jane beside him in the passenger seat. They’re closing in on her apartment complex.

Jane has the pair of wrist suspension cuffs in her lap. She holds one up between herself and Cade. “You’re sure it’s okay if I keep these?”

“Of course.” He confirms. “There’s plenty more where those came from.”

Jane sets the cuff back down in her lap, mulling over the evening. “So, what happened tonight? I could feel commotion in the room, but I couldn’t figure out what was going on.”

“Oh, this younger guy, he messed up and overdid it.”

“I hope he’s okay.”

“Yeah, I think he’ll be fine.”

“Do you need to get back for that, then?”

Cade turns into Jane’s apartment complex. He drives slowly through the parking lot in search of an empty stall. “They took him to the hospital, so I don’t see much else happening tonight,” he tells her. “Why?”

“I was going to invite you to spend the night.”

Cade pulls into a vacant parking spot and puts the truck in park. He stares straight ahead out the windshield. A moment passes, and then he heaves out a reserved sigh.

“What?” she asks self-consciously.

“I can’t do that.”

***

Later that night, a handful of stoned party guests are dispersed along the red booth seat in the smoky coffeeshop. The temple-like cabana seat in back is unoccupied. Across from it, Hannah saunters through the doorway. She melds into the peaceful energy in there right away, likely helped along by her pleasant alcohol buzz.

“Hello.” Hannah has a seat at the bar next to Cade. “When did you get back here?”

“Not even five minutes ago.”

Lo-fi electronic music beats rhythmically through the low-lit coffeeshop. Pam sits on a stool behind the bar, twisting the top on a metal grinder. She twists off the top and taps the sifted weed onto a tray on the bar.

Hannah looks over at the doorway and sees Reno walk in. “Oh.” She immediately livens up, waving him over. “Hey, come over here. Give me a cigarette.”

“Where are yours?” Reno strolls up to Hannah’s barstool and takes his pack out of his pocket.

“I’ve been bumming all night. Where am I gonna put a pack of cigarettes?” Hannah motions down at her stunning gold cocktail dress.

Reno pulls two cigarettes out of his pack. He hands one to Hannah.

“See, that wasn’t so hard.” She picks up a lighter off the bar and lights up. Reno takes the lighter from her.

“What a night.” He grunts before lighting up his cigarette.

“I assume you just got back from the hospital?” Cade asks him.

“Uh-huh.” Reno slides onto the barstool beside Hannah. “I got a ride back here.”

“Any news yet?”

“I didn’t stick around for long enough.” He subtly confesses to Cade. Still unwinding from the whole Trip mishap, Reno does his best to mask his tension. He leers down at the clean ashtray on the bar near Hannah, stumped by the fact there’s nothing in it. “Why is this empty?”

“We just got here. There’s a joint on the way.” Cade points to the end of the bar at the budtender, Ankh, a solid-built guy in his thirties.

That’s his cue. Ankh abruptly ends his conversation with Quinn, who’s seated in a barstool across from him. He bows respectfully at Cade and gets the tray of sifted weed from the bar in front of Pam. Ankh reaches under the counter for a rolling paper and a white cardboard tip.

Cade, Reno and Pam all quietly watch Ankh work. He’s highly regarded for his speed and aptitude at rolling a Dutch-style joint.

Hannah has a shorter attention span. She gazes over at the cabana seat at the end of the room. Then she whips around to Reno beside her. “Tell me what happened with Trip tonight. You walked in here when it was happening, right?”

“Yeah. I snuck in here to grab a joint, and I saw him starting to fall out.”

“Freaky.” She flicks her cigarette into the ashtray.

Behind the bar, Ankh nimbly rolls a cone-shaped joint. His intense dark eyes are fixed on the task at hand.

Reno blows a cloud of cigarette smoke up into the ceiling and looks down the bar at Cade. “So did he go take his brat Becky home, or what?”

“Who, Paul?”

“Yeah. It’s late enough that I figured he might be in here with you guys.”

“Ugh.” Hannah crinkles her forehead in amusement. She elbows Cade’s arm. “It sounds so funny when you call him ‘Paul’.”

“Not to me.”

“I’m sure.”

Ankh hands Cade the freshly rolled joint.

Cade smiles in appreciation and turns to Hannah. “I’ve called him Paul our whole lives. I’m not gonna suddenly start calling him a color.” He picks up a lighter sitting on the bar and lights the joint.

“No, I understand.” Hannah asserts to him. “We’re on the same page with the name thing, but it freaks me out every time. It’s the ONLY time I ever hear him called Paul.”

“Well, I refuse to call him anything else.” Cade restates and gets back to answering Reno’s question. “Anyway, I think he’s still here with her.”

***

He is in the main office with Random. They’re both seated behind the desk. The cream drapes are drawn closed on the window behind them.

Becky is across from them, sitting stiffly in a leather armchair. She has an empty hurricane glass on the desk in front of her. Becky skims back and forth between Black and Random.

“I think we’ve covered everything there is to say about the subject,” Random tells her.

“The thing I can’t get over is the timing.” She lays into Black. “I mean, Brian disappears from work, I meet you–”

“Totally unrelated.” He stops her right there.

“I don’t see how it can be. How did this happen at the exact same time, right after Brian and I broke it off?”

“But it didn’t, that’s the thing. You and I started talking months before that, and Brian just got involved here recently. I didn’t even make the connection until the day you quit your job.” Black explains.

“And that’s the other thing. If you knew, then why didn’t you warn me ahead of time?” she asks.

“I wasn’t even sure you’d cross paths with him.”

Becky wrinkles her nose at Black. “The entire situation just seems too weird. The day you were at my house, when you brought the picture of Brian into the kitchen and said that you tricked me into telling you who it was. What if that was all just part of it?”

“The bottom line, Becky, is if you can’t trust what I’m saying, then we have to end this.”

“Mm-hmm.” Random nods in solid agreement with him.

“No, that is not what I want.” She grows vehement.

“And I don’t want to keep having this conversation.” Black retorts.

“Okay. I’m sorry.” Becky recoils with a sigh. “It’s just really unbelievable.”

Random steps in and says, “What it is, is an unfortunate coincidence.”

She concentrates on Random across the desk.

“So, you’re gonna have to find a way to reconcile this, because there is no alternative.”

His words make a visible impact on Becky. To her, Random is an unbiased and fresh source of guidance.

“Don’t get in your own way, Becky. Don’t regress.” Random pragmatically advises her with a soft chuckle.

“Yeah, no. I know.” She emphasizes, making it clear that the last thing she wants is to go backwards in this process.

“We’re past the point of salvaging this night, so can I get you a ride home?” Black asks her.

Becky silently concedes. Then she sticks her hand up to stipulate. “Please not Reno though, please.”

***

Later that night, Jane is still wide awake. The lights in her living room are all off. The TV screen casts a reflection of a comedy movie onto her glass top coffee table. A dark couch with contrasting white pillows sits behind the coffee table. The wrist suspension cuffs are lying on one of the pillows.

She walks into the living room with a full glass of red wine. She sets the glass down on her coffee table and takes a seat on her couch. Jane fondles the suspension cuffs on the pillow. Her face reflects a pang of despondence about what went down in Cade’s SUV an hour earlier...

The truck is parked in front of Jane’s apartment building. The headlights are off, and the engine purrs quietly. Cade drums his fingers on the steering wheel.

In the passenger seat, Jane puts the suspension cuffs down on the floor mat. She slides in over the center console to Cade, who puts his arm around her shoulders and draws her in close.

Jane leans against him, placing her hand on his chest. “Nothing has to happen.” She rests her temple on his shoulder. “I just want you to stay.”

Cade grimaces, undoubtedly conflicted. “Something would definitely happen.” After a brief smile he adds, “And I can’t risk getting caught up in the moment.”

“You can’t temporarily divert from the plan?” She glimpses up at Cade to see him shaking his head. “All I really want is to wake up next to you.”

“I want to spend more time with you too, Jane, I do. But I’m not good enough.”

“I don’t understand.”

“I haven’t done this as much as my colleagues have. For myself, I mean. I haven’t really done it at all.”

“I’m actually glad to hear that.” She runs her palm across Cade’s chest. “And I’m even more impressed with what I’ve seen, so far.”

“I shouldn’t even be telling you this, honestly.”

Jane lifts her head from Cade’s shoulder to reassure him. “Really though. I’m glad that I’m not just one of many, for you. I really am.”

***

“You actually told her all of that?” The Sunday morning hot tub ritual is in full swing. Black is seated with his back to the house and a stunned expression on his face.

“Unfortunately, yes. But at least I didn’t spend the night.” Cade sticks up for himself. “I came back here and hung out with you in the coffeeshop.”

Hannah glares at Cade, awash with disapproval. “You weak-willed, blazing idiot. You showed her your hand?”

“I wasn’t in my role. I was taking her home.”

“First time out the gate and you crap your pants.” She snarls at him. “You’re an embarrassment.”

“I know.” Cade hangs his head in shame. “I might make a good Top, but I’m a subpar Dom.”

Hannah’s right brow arches up in question. She reaches back and grabs her morning banana. “I’ve never really thought of you as a hallmark Top, either.”

Black initially concurs with Hannah and then stops. “Wait, what’s the difference?” He contemplates while Cade gets defensive, and Hannah starts peeling her banana.

“Hey, come on, I’m not that bad.” Cade shifts over and sinks down into the corner of the tub. Water bubbles around his jawline as the jets work his neck.

“Oh, never mind you.” Hannah spins to Black. “What’s going on with Becky?” She finishes peeling the skin on her banana. “She saw Brian?”

“She did,” Black tells Hannah, who takes a bite of her banana. Cade furtively watches her.

Hannah swallows before asking, “And?”

“It put her in a state, so I took her into the office to talk. And Random was already in there, of course.”

“What for?” Cade asks.

Black gives him an annoyed shrug. “Who knows, but it probably seemed to her like I planned it.”

“Ganging up on her, yeah.” Hannah continues eating her banana.

“Exactly.”

“Remind me,” Cade prods Black, “why didn’t you tell her that her ex would be there?”

“If you factor in Hannah’s subordinate turnover lately, there was at least a decent chance he wouldn’t be there. Let’s be honest.”

Cade cracks up, dunking his entire chin under the water. “That’s true.”

“The thing is, I want to get upset, but I can’t.” Hannah admits. “It makes total sense that you would entertain that possibility.” She squeezes the last bite of banana into her mouth and proceeds to chuck the empty peel behind her.

“Right, the problem could have resolved itself before it even occurred.”

“All right.” Hannah shoots Black a dirty look. The empty banana peel sails over her shoulder. “I agreed, so let’s not drive the point home further, okay?” She stretches her tan arms out along the sides of the tub.

“That was generous of you.” Cade plays up to Hannah before switching the subject.

“I know it was.”

“So.” He glances over at Black. “Did Reno ever catch up with you last night? It seemed like he wanted to talk to you.”

“No, I didn’t see him.”

“Speaking of Reno.” Hannah swoops in towards Cade. “He looked rattled to me, last night.”

“Yeah, I think the Trip thing stressed him out.”

“I don’t think I’ve ever seen Reno stressed before,” she mentions, “it was weird. Very subtle but weird.”

***

Canary-yellow lilies run from the side entrance door to the front of the Mercer Estate, in a landscaped area alongside it. They’re much more noticeable in the light of day. On the other side of the door is a rock bed that runs to the back of the house. Inside that rock bed are a few displays of carefully balanced rocks. One display is a small arch. Another is a 2’ tall stack of alternating large and small rocks.

Further down the rock bed, Reno is seated by his latest display with his back to the wooded area. He’s balancing small round rocks between medium-sized oblong ones. Highly absorbed, Reno appears almost motionless as he rotates the small round rock between his fingers. He holds the top, oblong rock still while leisurely gauging the weight and position of the two rocks. This is his meditation.

Reno rolls his eyes up to the sky. He enters a moment of clarity. “Oh.” Exulted, he tosses the two rocks aside. He digs into his pocket for his phone and calls Quinn. “Quinn, I’ve got it.” Reno stands up and paces in front of the rock bed.

“You figured out a way to make the cage smaller?” she asks on the other line.

“Yes.”

“Tell me about it.”

“Eliminate the bars.”

“Then it ceases to be a cage, doesn’t it?”

“Just meet me down in the workshop.” Reno steps up to the side door and heads inside...

The fluorescent lights are on in the nicely equipped workshop area. Vertical shelving units contain sheets of Plexiglas, MDO board and plywood. Next to the shelving units, lumber is piled up on a storage rack. Mounted on the wall are commercial-sized coils of various ropes, chains and cables.

There’s a forklift parked in the corner. Nearby the forklift are the larger tools, including a table saw, an upright sheet cutter and an air compressor. On the floor beside the air compressor is a series of grey metal toolboxes and storage cabinets.

A carpet-covered table runs down the middle of the workshop across from the doors, which swing open. Reno and Quinn walk inside.

“Wow.” Reno gleans the workshop, surprised. “We’ve got the place to ourselves. I can’t believe Andrew and Eric aren’t in here.”

“Maybe Sunday is their sexy day.”

“Sexy Sunday.” After putting his sarcastic slant on it, Reno follows Quinn over to the carpet-covered worktable in the middle of the room.

“They could just be at brunch.” She leans back against the table. Behind her, a workbench lines the length of one wall in the shop. Above it is a pegboard with hooks that store an organized variety of tools ranging from hammers and screwdrivers to cordless drills and nail guns. “So then,” Quinn picks Reno’s brain, “tell me about this cage with no bars.”

Reno crouches down to the shelves below the table. He takes out a 2’ long 4”x4” post and sets it upright on its end on top of the table. “We keep the basic cage idea that he wants, but like I said, we remove the bars. We just put these in the four corners.” Reno places his palm on the top end of the post. “That way, the top can just go on a hinge.”

“Okay.” Quinn grows pensive as she runs with his idea. “What are you thinking for tie-off points?”

He taps the bottom of the post. “I’m thinking I’ll drill a one-inch hole diagonally through the top and bottom of each post.”

“Ah,” Quinn ponders, “and fish rope through.”

“Right. What do you think?”

“It’s good. Let’s do it.” Quinn pushes off of the worktable and goes over to the lumber storage rack.

Reno roams over to the vertical shelving unit. He pulls out a 4’x8’ sheet of clear Plexiglas.

“I think we should smooth out the posts and round off the corners. When you get them cut down, I’ll go over them with the palm sander.” Quinn takes a 4”x4” post off the storage rack and moves it over to the edge of the worktable.

Reno carries the Plexiglas over to the sheet cutter and sets it into the bottom channel. “What’s the situation you’re in with Black’s new recruit?” he asks on his way back over to the worktable. He stoops down to the shelves below the table and grabs a tape measure and pencil.

Quinn returns to the lumber storage rack to retrieve a second 4”x4” post. “I’m going to be her governess.”

“You’re training her?”

“Who better than me?” She slides the second post onto the worktable.

Reno hooks the tape measure on the end of the first post, measuring down three feet. “There is nobody better than you for that sort of thing.” He marks it at three feet and continues pulling the tape further down the post. “How’s it going?”

“I just met her last night.” Quinn saunters over to the workbench along the wall. She scans the pegboard for a palm sander.

“What do you make of her?”

Quinn scowls at him over her shoulder. “Oh now, stop. You know I don’t gossip.” She turns back to the pegboard and takes a palm sander off the wall.

“Come on, Quinn.” Reno measures down to six feet and marks the post. “I’d like to consider us friends.”

She spins away from the workbench and heads back over to Reno. Sporting a feisty smile, he hooks the tape measure on the end of the second post.

“Knock it off, Reno. You’re just as bad as Hannah. You two are exactly the same. Beautiful nosy people.” Quinn sets the palm sander on the worktable. “Can we just get back to work? This is my happy place these days, you know?”

Reno marks the post at three feet and sneers at Quinn. “So, you don’t like her.”

“I did not say that.” She softens up before explaining. “I’m just gonna be putting in a lot more hours because of her.”

“He’s moving her in here?”

***

Becky sits on her desk chair in the living room of her townhouse later that morning. She faces Black, who’s camped out in the corner of her couch.

He pops the lid off of the coffee he’s holding and takes a drink. “It was a rough night for everybody.” Black sets his coffee down on the long table behind the couch.

Becky bobs her head, fully agreeing with him.

“You got some disturbing news about Brian.”

“Yes. Yes, I did.”

He looks at her. “Knowing what you know now, do you want in?”

Becky hesitates. She tilts forward in her chair, replaying the question in her mind to make sure she heard it correctly. “In the house we were at last night? Your house?”

“My house, along with a hundred other people including Brian.”

“Yes.” She tenaciously snaps up straight in her chair. “Yes, that’s what I’ve been wanting.”

“It’s a big change, so make sure you think it over.”

“I’ve already thought it over.” She claims, thick with determination. “When can I make it happen?”

“That’s up to you and when you can be ready.”

Becky flings her hands up in the air. “I have all day.” She pauses in reflection. “Did you say a hundred people live there?” She lowers her hands and grips onto her thighs.

“Give or take. That said, you need to be selective about what you bring. You can only pack what will fit into a furnished, modest-sized bedroom. That’s it.” He instructs her. “Leave everything else here as it is.”

The sound of Hannah crunching on popcorn is the only noise in the surveillance room. Becky’s chattering face fills the monitor on the wall.

Hannah yanks out her earbuds and rants to Cade. “She is tame.” She reaches for her can of soda on the counter. “Where is this impetuous fireball Becky I’ve been hearing so much about?” She takes a drink.

“She’s not in control right now, and she knows that. This is not the time for her to rock the boat.”

“That sucks.” Bummed out, Hannah sets her soda back down on the counter.

Beside her, Cade is relaxed in his chair and focused on the monitor. The meeting has been dragging on for almost half an hour.

“This isn’t much of a show, and I’m trapped in here, now.” Hannah eyeballs the secret doorway.

“Not for much longer. Black has a job to get to. And I can tell Random wants to wrap this up, badly.” Cade notes...

On the other side of the secret bookcase door, the rich glow of early evening illuminates the window behind Black and Random. Becky’s white folder is lying open on the desk in front of her.

“So what about–”

Random cuts Becky off with a wave of his hand. “It’s all in there, I promise you.”

“We’ve all been where you’re at right now. That’s the purpose of this.” Black motions to the white folder. “I challenge you to find a question that hasn’t been answered somewhere in there.”

Becky closes the folder and picks it up. “I guess if all the answers to my questions are in here, I’ll just read it instead of taking up any more of your time.”

“Excellent.” Random is outright thrilled to hear her say that. He dryly adds, “Oh, and welcome to the party.”

Becky clutches the folder to her chest and watches Black stand up from his chair. His lean body towers over the desk, asking her,

“Ready to get started?”
